Al-Hasan, Abu 'Amr, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Humayd and Ibn Kathir, in the narration of al-Bazzi, read min Saba'a, with both hamzas open and without tanwin, treating it as the name of a tribe; this is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd. The rest read it in the genitive (min Saba'in), taking it as the name of a man. The report also states that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about Saba', and he said: "He was a man who had ten sons; six of them were on the right and four on the left." We will mention their names and their story in Surat Saba', God willing, the Mighty and Majestic. And the poet said:

"The Wariddun and Taym are at the peaks of Saba,
the buffalo hide has bitten their necks."

[bi-naba'in yaqin] (with certain news): with news that there is no doubt in.

Wahb said: The hoopoe said: "I have found a king whom your kingdom has not reached."

[Inni wajadtu imra'atan tamlikuhum] (Indeed I found a woman ruling them). Her name was Bilqis, daughter of al-Sharah, who is al-Hudhadh. It was said: Sharahil ibn Dhi Hadan ibn al-Yashrij ibn al-Harith ibn Qays ibn Sufa ibn Saba ibn Yashkhub ibn Ya'rub ibn Qahtan. Bilqis's father, who was called al-Yashrij and nicknamed al-Hudhadh, was a king of great station; forty kings were born to him, and he ruled all the land of Yemen. He used to say to the kings of the outlying regions: "None of you is my equal." He refused to marry among them, so they married him to a woman from the jinn called Rayhana, daughter of al-Sakan, and she bore him Tilmaqa, who is Bilqis; he had no child other than her.

This is confirmed by what:

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hurim ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Qatadah, from al-Nadr ibn Anas, from Bishr ibn Nahik, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "One of Bilqis's two parents was a jinn."

They said: When the father of Bilqis died, leaving no child other than her, she coveted the kingdom and asked her people to pledge allegiance to her. Some obeyed her and others disobeyed her, so they chose a man over her and made him king over them. They split into two factions, each faction taking control of a region of the land of Yemen with its kingdom.

Then this man whom they had made king behaved badly towards the people of his kingdom, to the point that he would reach out his hand to the women of his subjects and commit fornication with them. His companions wanted to depose him, but they could not overpower him. When Bilqis saw that, jealousy seized her, and she sent to him offering herself to him. The king replied: "By God, what prevented me from beginning with a proposal to you was only my despair of you." She said: "I am not averse to you, for you are a noble match. Gather the men of my people and propose to me before them." He gathered them and proposed to her before them. They said: "We do not think she will do this." He said to them: "Rather, it is she who initiated with me, so I want you to hear her words and bear witness against her." When they came to her and mentioned that to her, she said: "Yes, I wanted a husband and I never ceased to; I was averse to this before, but now I am content with him, so marry me to him." When she was conducted to him, she went out with many people of her servants and retinue, until his residences and houses were filled with them. When she came to him, she gave him wine until he became drunk, then she cut off his head and returned at night to her dwelling. When the people awoke, they saw the king slain with his head set up at the gate of her house, and they knew that that marriage had been deceit and treachery on her part. They gathered to her and said: "You are more worthy of this kingdom than anyone else." She said: "Had it not been for shame and disgrace, I would not have killed him, but his corruption had spread, and zeal seized me until I did what I did." So they made her queen, and her affair was established.[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/211, with variations.]] [110]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Khadijah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi al-Layth narrated to us in Baghdad, saying: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Muslim, from al-Hasan, from Abu Bakrah, who said: Bilqis was mentioned in the presence of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "A people who entrust their affairs to a woman will never prosper."[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/211.]] [111]

[Wa-utiyat min kulli shay'] (And she had been given of everything): of what kings need in terms of equipment and provisions.

[Wa-laha 'arshun 'azim] (And she has a mighty throne): a huge, fine throne. Its front was of gold inlaid with red rubies and green emeralds, and its back was of silver adorned with various kinds of jewels. It had four legs: one of red ruby, one of emerald, one of green ruby, and one of pearl; the panels of the throne were of gold, and upon it were seven doors, each chamber having a closed door.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Bilqis's throne was thirty cubits by thirty cubits, and its height in the air was thirty cubits.

Muqatil said: It was eighty cubits by thirty cubits, and its height in the air was eighty cubits, adorned with jewels.

[Wajadtuha wa-qawmaha yasjudna lil-shams min duni Allah] (I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of God), [wa-zayyana lahumu al-shaytanu a'malahum fa-sadahum 'ani al-sabili fa-hum la yahtadun] (and Satan adorned for them their deeds and barred them from the path, so they are not guided), [alla yasjudu lillah] (that they should not prostrate to God). Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Balkhi, al-Hasan, Abu Ja'far, Humayd, al-A'raj, al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub, in the narration of Ruways, read "ala usjudu" with a light (takhfif) pronunciation, in the sense of: "Ala, O people, prostrate!", taking it as a command from God, the Exalted, begun anew, and omitting "ya ha'ula'" (O you people) as indicated by its agent. Some have cited from the Arabs by report: "Ala ya arhamuna" (Ah, O have mercy on us!), "Ala ya tasaddaqu 'alayna" (Ah, O give alms to us!), meaning "Ala ya qawm" (O people), like the saying of al-Akhtal:

"Ala ya Salma, ya Hind, Hind of the Banu Badr,
even if our neighbour has passed away, it is forever."

According to this reading, "usjudu" is in the jussive position as a command, and one pauses on "ala," then begins "usjudu."

Al-Farra' said: Al-Kisa'i narrated to me from 'Isa al-Hamadhani, who said: I never heard the shaykhs reading it except with light pronunciation, intending the imperative. It appears in the reading of 'Abd Allah as "hal-la tasjudu lillah" with the ta', and in the reading of Ubayy as "ala yasjudna lillah." These two readings are proof for those who read it lightly. The rest read "alla yasjudu" with emphasis (tashdid), meaning: [wa-zayyana lahumu al-shaytanu a'malahum] (Satan adorned for them their deeds) so that they would not prostrate to God. "Allā" is in the accusative position, and "yasjudu" is in the accusative by "an." Abu 'Ubayd chose this reading and said: "The light pronunciation has a good aspect, but in it the report is cut off from the matter of Saba' and its people, and then it returns after to mention them; whereas the reading with emphasis is a continuous report, one part following another, with no break in its middle. The pause is on 'ala' and then one begins 'yasjudu,' just as one connects [alladhi yukhriju al-khab'a]."

[Alladhi yukhriju al-khab'a fi al-samawati wal-ard] (He who brings forth the hidden in the heavens and the earth): meaning the unseen of the heavens and the earth.

Most exegetes said: the hidden of the heaven is rain, and the hidden of the earth is plants. In the reading of 'Abd Allah: "yukhriju al-khab'a min al-samawat," and "min" and "fi" are interchangeable. The Arabs say: "La-astakhrijanna al-'ilma fikum," meaning "minkum" (from you). This is related by al-Farra'.

[Wa-ya'lamu ma yukhfuna wa-ma yu'linun] (And He knows what they conceal and what they proclaim): the common reading has the verbs with "ya" in both, while al-Kisa'i read them with "ta," and this is the narration of Hafs from 'Asim.

[Allahu la ilaha illa huwa rabbu al-'arshi al-'azim] (God—there is no god but He, Lord of the Mighty Throne): the throne, however great it is, is inferior to Him; no throne resembles Him, neither the throne of the queen of Saba' nor any other.

Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Zayd said: From His saying [ahatu bima lam tuhit bihi] up to His saying [la ilaha illa huwa rabbu al-'arshi al-'azim], the whole is the speech of the hoopoe.

And We gave David and Solomon knowledge, and they said, "Praise be to God, who has favoured us above many of His believing servants." ﴿And Solomon inherited David.﴾ He inherited his prophethood, his knowledge and his kingship, to the exclusion of David's other sons, and David had nineteen sons.

Muqatil said: Solomon had greater kingship than David and was more judicious than him, while David was more devoted in worship than Solomon (peace be upon them both).

﴿And Solomon said,﴾ giving thanks for the blessings of God, the Glorified and Exalted, upon him: "O people, we have been taught the speech of the birds," meaning that God made their speech like the speech of the children of Adam, since he understood it from them, "and we have been given of everything. Indeed, this is evidently a great favour."

Muqatil said concerning this verse: Solomon (peace be upon him) was sitting when a bird flew past him. He said to his companions, "Do you know what the bird that passed by us is saying?" They said, "You know best." Solomon said, "It said to me:

'Peace be upon you, O king who holds power over the Children of Israel. May God, the Glorified and Exalted, grant you honour and give you victory over your enemy. I am going to my young, and then I will pass by you again.'

And it will return to us a second time, so watch its return."

He said: The people looked for a long time, and then it passed by them and said, "Peace be upon you, O king. If you will permit me, I will gather food for my young until they grow up, and then I will come to you, and do with me what you wish." Solomon informed them of what it had said, and he gave it permission.

Farqad al-Sakhi said: Solomon passed by a nightingale on a tree, moving its head and tilting its tail. He said to his companions, "Do you know what this nightingale is saying?" They said, "God and His Prophet know best." He said, "It is saying: 'I ate half a date, so let the world be forgotten.'"

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-'Adl informed me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanbah and Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan narrated to us, both saying: al-Fadl ibn al-'Abbas al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying:

Musa ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: 'Abbad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from al-Kalbi, from a man, from Ka'b, who said:

A turtledove cried out in the presence of Solomon ibn Dawud (peace be upon him), and he said, "Do you know what it is saying?"
They said, "No."
He said, "It is saying: [[In the second manuscript (Isfahan) there is an addition: 'Build for death and construct for ruin.' A dove cried out in the presence of Solomon, and he said: "Do you know what it is saying?" They said, "No." He said, "It is saying:"]] 'Would that these creatures had not been created.'"

A peacock cried out in the presence of Solomon (peace be upon him), and he said, "Do you know what it is saying?"
They said, "No."
He said, "It is saying [[In the second manuscript there is an addition: 'As you judge, so you will be judged.' A hoopoe cried out in the presence of Solomon, and he said: "Do you know what it is saying?" They said, "No." He said, "It is saying:"]] 'Whoever does not show mercy will not be shown mercy.'"

A sparrow-hawk (sard) cried out in the presence of Solomon, and he said, "Do you know what it is saying?"
They said, "No."
He said, "It is saying: 'Seek forgiveness from God, O sinners.' For this reason the Messenger of God (ﷺ) forbade killing it."

Then a tuttuwa (a small bird) cried out in the presence of Solomon (peace be upon him), and he said, "Do you know what it is saying?"
They said, "No."
He said, "It is saying: 'Every living thing will die, and every new thing will decay.'"

A swallow cried out in the presence of Solomon (peace be upon him), and he said, "Do you know what it is saying?"
They said, "No."
He said, "It is saying: 'Send forward good, and you will find it.' For this reason the Messenger of God (ﷺ) forbade killing it."

A dove cooed in the presence of Solomon (peace be upon him), and he said, "Do you know what this dove is saying?" They said, "No."
He said, "It is saying: 'Glory be to my Lord, the Most High, whose heaven and earth are full of Him.'"

A Qumri (a type of dove) cried out in the presence of Solomon (peace be upon him), and he said, "Do you know what it is saying?"
They said, "No."
He said, "It is saying: 'Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.' The raven calls down curses upon the tax collector. The kite says: 'Everything perishes except God.' The sand partridge says: 'Whoever keeps silent is safe.' The parrot says: 'Woe to him whose concern is the world.' The frog says: 'Glory be to my Lord, the Holy.' The falcon says: 'Glory be to my Lord and praise be to Him.' The female frog says: 'Glory be to the One who is remembered in every place.'"

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan narrated to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn al-'Abbas ibn Mihran narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Isma'il informed us, from 'Ayyash, from Zirr, from Makhul, who said: A partridge cried out in the presence of Solomon ibn Dawud (peace be upon him), and he said, "Do you know what it is saying?"
They said, "No."
He said, "It is saying: 'The Most Merciful settled Himself upon the Throne.'"

And with its chain from Musa ibn Ibrahim, who said: Salih al-Harawi informed us, from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When the rooster crows, it is saying: 'Remember God, O heedless ones.'" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/166.]] [108]

Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, who said: When the vulture cries out, it says: "O son of Adam, live as you wish, its end is death." When the eagle cries out, it says: "In distance from people is companionship." When the qabbar (a type of bird) cries out, it says: "My God, curse those who hate the family of Muhammad." When the swallow cries out, it recites: ﴿Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds﴾, prolonging the "ḍāllīn" (the final word, "those who go astray") as a reciter would prolong it.

﴿And for Solomon were gathered his armies of jinn and humans and birds, and they were marshalled in ranks.﴾ That is, they were gathered and assembled for him on a march, "so they were kept in order," meaning that the first of them was held back until the last of them had gathered. This was because he placed over each category of them guards (wuzʿah) who restrained the front of them until the rear caught up, so that they would not advance ahead in the march, as kings do.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "yūza'ūn" means "they are pushed back." Ibn Zayd and Muqatil said: "They are driven." Al-Suddi said: "They are made to stop." The root of wazʿ in the Arabic language is restraint and prevention, and from it comes the hadith: "The ruler restrains more than the Qur'an restrains." It is also said, "awza'ahu al-amr," meaning he charged him with the matter.

In a report: "People must have guards (wuzʿah)." And a poet said:

"When I rebuked the greying hair for my youth, and said: 'Would that I were sound, but the greying hair is a restrainer.'" [[Lisan al-'Arab: 4/83.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Talhah ibn Muhammad and 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad narrated to us, both saying: Abu Bakr ibn Mujahid narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sunayd narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Abu Ma'shar, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, concerning this verse, who said: It has reached us that Solomon's army was a hundred farsakhs (a unit of distance): twenty-five of them were for humans, twenty-five for jinn, twenty-five for wild animals, and twenty-five for birds. He had a thousand tents of glass upon wooden frames, in which were three hundred wives and seven hundred concubines. He commanded the violent wind, and it carried him, and he commanded the gentle wind, and it moved him along. It was revealed to him, while he was travelling between heaven and earth: "I have increased your kingdom: no creature will speak a word, but the wind will come and inform you of it."

Muqatil said: The devils wove for Solomon (peace be upon him) a carpet one farsakh by one farsakh, of gold woven into silk. A golden pulpit was placed for him in the middle of the carpet, and he sat upon it, and around him were three thousand thrones of gold and silver. The prophets sat on golden thrones, the scholars on silver thrones, and the people surrounded them, and around the people were the jinn and the devils. The birds shaded him with their wings so that the sun would not fall upon him, and the east wind lifted the carpet, travelling a month's distance from morning to afternoon and from afternoon to morning.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Malik al-Qati'i narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ayyub narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr, that is Ibn 'Ayyash, narrated to us, from Idris ibn Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: My father told me that Solomon (peace be upon him) once rode the sea. He passed by a farmer, who looked at him and said: "The family of David has been given a great kingdom." The wind carried his words to Solomon's ear, so he descended and came to the farmer and said: "I have heard your words, and I came to you only so that you would not wish for what you cannot attain. One single glorification that God, the Exalted, accepts is better than what the family of David has been given." The farmer said: "May God remove your worry as you have removed mine."

﴿Until, when they came upon the valley of the ants.﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Makhlad ibn Ja'far [[In the second manuscript there is an addition: al-Baqawi.]] narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Alawiyyah narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn 'Isa narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Abu Ilyas informed us, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, from Ka'b, who said: When Solomon (peace be upon him) rode, he carried his family and all his retinue, his servants and scribes, in those canopies one above another according to their ranks. He had kitchens and bakeries carried with him, with iron ovens and large cooking pots, each capable of holding the contents of ten slaughtered camels. He had arenas for the animals set out in front of him. Cooks cooked, bakers baked, and the animals ran before him between heaven and earth, while the wind swept them along.

He travelled with those who accompanied him toward Yemen, and he took the route through Madinah, the city of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Solomon said: "This is the abode of emigration of a prophet at the end of time. Blessed is whoever believes in him, blessed is whoever follows him, and blessed is whoever takes him as a model." He saw around the House (the Ka'bah) idols being worshipped apart from God, the Glorified. When Solomon passed by the House, the House wept. God, the Glorified, revealed to the House: "What makes you weep?" It said: "My Lord, a prophet of Yours and a people of Your friends passed by me, but they did not descend in me, they did not pray at me, and they did not mention You in my presence, while idols are worshipped around me apart from You." God, the Glorified, revealed to it: "Do not weep, for I will fill you with prostrating faces, and I will send down in you a new Qur'an, and I will raise up from you a prophet at the end of time, the most beloved of My prophets to Me. I will place in you people from My creation who will worship Me, and I will prescribe for My servants an obligation, so that they will hasten to you as eagles hasten to their nests, and yearn for you as a she-camel yearns for her young and a dove for her egg. I will purify you from idols and the worshippers of Satan."

He said: Then Solomon proceeded until he passed through the Valley of Sadir, a valley of al-Ta'if. He came upon the valley of the ants, and a single ant was walking, and it was lame, limping, and it was as large as a male... in size. The ant called out: ﴿O ants, enter your dwellings, lest Solomon and his armies crush you without their perceiving it.﴾ This means that Solomon understood its speech, and no creature spoke except that the wind carried it and cast it into the ears of Solomon (peace be upon him).

He said: ﴿So he smiled, laughing at its speech, and said: "My Lord, grant me the ability to be grateful for Your blessing..." up to His words: "among Your righteous servants."﴾ That is, "among Your monotheist servants."

Qatadah and Muqatil said: The valley of the ants was in the land of Syria.

Nawf al-Himyari said: The ants of the valley of Solomon were like flies.

al-Sha'bi said: The ant whose speech Solomon understood had two wings.

Muqatil said: Solomon heard its speech from three miles away. They differed about the name of that ant.

Abu 'Abd Allah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Husayni al-Dinawari informed me, saying: Abu al-'Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Sarsari narrated to us, saying: al-Haytham ibn Khalaf al-Duri narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn Hatim al-Bazzaz narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Zabarqan al-Taymi narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, who said: The name of the ant that spoke to Solomon ibn Dawud (peace be upon him) was Tahiyah.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Talhah and 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Mujahid narrated to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abu Muhammad al-Nu'man ibn Shibl al-Bahili narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Rawq narrated to us, from his father, who said: The name of Solomon's ant was Harami, and this is the saying of Muqatil.

I saw in some books that when Solomon heard the speech of the ant, he said: "Bring her to me." They brought her to him, and he said to her: "Why did you warn the ants against my injustice? Do you not know that I am a just prophet? Why did you say: 'Lest Solomon and his armies crush you'?" The ant said: "Did you not hear my words: 'without their perceiving it'? Moreover, I did not intend the crushing of souls, but the crushing of hearts. I feared that they would long for what you have been given and would occupy themselves with looking rather than with glorification." He said to her: "Advise me." The ant said: "Do you know why your father was named David?" He said: "No." She said: "Because he treated his wound and it healed." "Do you know why you were named Solomon?" He said: "No." She said: "Because you are sound (salim), and you were given what you were given because of the soundness of your heart, and you are destined to join your father." Then she said: "Do you know why God subjected the wind to you?" He said: "No." She said: "God has informed you that the whole world is wind." So Solomon smiled, laughing in wonder at her speech, and said: "My Lord, grant me the ability..." to the end of the verse.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah informed us, saying: al-Hadrami informed us, saying: Hasan al-Khallal narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) forbade the killing of four kinds of animals: the hoopoe, the sparrow-hawk, the bee, and the ant.

﴿And he inspected the birds﴾, that is, he sought them and searched for them. ﴿And said: "Why do I not see the hoopoe? Or is it among the absent?"﴾ Ibn Kathir, 'Asim, al-Kisa'i and Ayyub read the (lī, "to me") here and in Surat Ya-Sin, "wa mā lī lā a'budu" [[Surat Ya-Sin: 22.]]. Hamzah read the yā' in both places (as a lengthened vowel). As for Abu 'Amr, he read the yā' in this place but read it with a fatḥah in Ya-Sin, and he distinguished between them, saying: "Because the one here is a question, and the other is a negation."

"Am" (or) here: it is said the mīm is an added particle. It is also said that "am" here means "bal" (rather), so the meaning is "rather, was he among the absent?"

﴿I will surely punish him with a severe punishment.﴾ His punishment would be that his feathers and tail be plucked out, leaving him bare, and then he would be thrown into an ant-hill so that the ants would bite him. 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad said: "Plucking and exposing him to the sun."
al-Dahhak: "I will tie his leg tightly and expose him to the sun."
Muqatil ibn Hayyan: "I will coat him with tar and expose him to the sun."
It is also said: "I will confine him in a cage." It is also said: "I will separate him from his mate." It is also said: "I will prevent him from serving me." It is also said: "I will scatter him."

﴿Or I will slaughter him, or he will bring me a clear authority.﴾ That is, a manifest proof.

As for the reason for Solomon's searching for the hoopoe and asking about it among the birds, it was that it neglected the turn of duty it was assigned, and Solomon (peace be upon him) needed water. He did not know where the water was. It was said to him: "The knowledge of that is with the hoopoe." He searched for it, did not find it, and threatened it. The story concerning it, as the scholars of the lives of the prophets have related, has intermingled accounts of some with others:

When the Prophet of God, Solomon (ﷺ), finished building the Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), he resolved to set out for the land of the Haram. He prepared for the journey and took with him humans, jinn, devils, birds and wild animals, until his army reached a hundred farsakhs. He commanded the gentle wind, and it carried them. When he arrived at the Haram and remained there as long as God willed him to remain, he slaughtered each day, during his stay, a total of five thousand camels, five thousand bulls and twenty thousand sheep.

He said to the notables of his people who were present: "This is a place from which a prophet of Arab origin will come forth, whose description is such and such. He will be given victory over all who oppose him, and his awe will reach a distance of a month's journey, the near and the far being equal in his sight in truth, and he will not be deterred by the blame of any blamer concerning God."

They said: "Then which religion shall we follow, O Prophet of God?" He said: "The religion of the Hanifiyyah (the pure monotheism of Abraham). Blessed is whoever reaches him, believes in him and affirms him."

They said: "How far is it between us and his coming forth, O Prophet of God?" He said: "About a thousand years. Let the present among you inform the absent, for he is the master of the prophets and the seal of the messengers, and his name is Muhammad among the company of the prophets."

He remained in Mecca until he had completed his rites. Then he wished to go to the land of Yemen. He left Mecca in the morning and travelled toward Yemen on the day the star Suhayl rose. He reached Sana'a at midday, and that was a month's journey. He saw a land whose greenness was flourishing, and he wished to alight there to pray and to take his midday meal. They sought water and did not find any, and the hoopoe was his guide to water. It could see the water beneath the earth as one of you sees his cup in his hand. It would peck the earth and know the place of the water and its depth, and then the devils would come and dig it out as a skin is flayed, and then they would extract the water.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Ibn 'Abbas mentioned this report, and Nafi' ibn al-Azraq said to him: "You claim that the hoopoe pecks the earth and sees the water. How can it see this and not see the two grains of wheat that fall around its neck?"

Ibn 'Abbas said to him: "Woe to you! When destiny comes, it intervenes between the sight and what it sees."

Qatadah narrated from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Do not kill the hoopoe, for it was Solomon's guide to the nearness and distance of water, and it loved that God be worshipped on the earth, as it said: ﴿And I have come to you from Saba' with certain news. Indeed, I found a woman...﴾" the verse.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 27, verse 15–26 (part 2 of 2):

They said: When Sulayman descended, the hoopoe said: "Sulayman has become occupied with descending, so ascend towards the sky and look at the length and breadth of the world." So he did that, and he looked to the right and to the left, and he saw a garden and inclined towards the greenery and landed in it. Suddenly he found a hoopoe, and he descended upon it. The name of the hoopoe of Sulayman ibn Dawud (peace be upon him) was Ya'fur, and the name of the hoopoe of Yemen was 'Anfar [[It is also narrated: 'Anfir and 'Anqar.]]. So 'Anfar said to Ya'fur, the hoopoe of Sulayman: "From where have you come, and where are you heading?"

He said: "I have come from al-Sham with my master Sulayman ibn Dawud (peace be upon him)."

The hoopoe said: "And who is Sulayman ibn Dawud?" He said: "The king of the jinn, the humans, the devils, the birds, the beasts and the wind. So where are you from?" He said: "I am from these lands." He said: "And who rules them?" He said: "A woman called Bilqis. Your master Sulayman has a great kingdom, but the kingdom of Bilqis is not inferior to it. She has taken possession of the whole sun, and under her hands are twelve thousand commanders, and under the hand of each commander are a hundred thousand fighters."

"Will you go with me so that you may see her kingdom?" He said: "I fear that Sulayman will look for me at the time of prayer when I need water."

The Yemeni hoopoe said: "Your master would be glad that you bring him news of this queen." So he set out with him, and he looked at Bilqis and her kingdom, and he did not return to Sulayman except at the time of 'Asr.

He said: When Sulayman descended and entered upon his place at the time of prayer, he sought the hoopoe, for he had landed in a place without water. He asked the humans about water, and they said: "We know of no water here." He asked the jinn and the devils, and they did not know either. Then he searched for the hoopoe and did not find it. Ibn 'Abbas said, in some narrations: and he became weary from searching the sun [for it]. Sulayman looked, and saw that the place of the hoopoe was empty. So he called the chief of the birds, who is the eagle (al-nasr), and asked him about the hoopoe. He said: "May God set the king right, I do not know where it is, and I have not sent it to any place." At that, Sulayman (peace be upon him) became angry and said: "I will surely punish it with a severe punishment, or I will surely slaughter it, or it shall bring me a clear authority."

'Ikrimah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Every 'sultan' in the Qur'an means proof."

They said: Then he called the hawk, the lord of the birds, and said: "Bring me the hoopoe at once." So the hawk raised itself above the sky until it settled in the air, and it looked at the world like a bowl before one of you, then it turned to the right and to the left, and suddenly it saw the hoopoe approaching from the direction of Yemen. The hawk swooped down towards it, intending it. When the hoopoe saw that, it knew that the hawk was aiming at it with harm, so it implored it, saying: "By the right of God who gave you strength and empowered you over me, have mercy on me and do not harm me."

So the hawk turned away from it and said to it: "Woe to you, may your mother be bereaved! The prophet of God has sworn that he will punish you or slaughter you." Then they both flew towards Sulayman. When it reached the army, the eagle and the birds met it and said to it: "Woe to you! Where were you absent in this sleep of yours? The prophet of God has threatened you, and they informed him of what he had said."

The hoopoe said: "Did the Messenger of God not make an exception?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Or he shall bring me a clear excuse." Then the hawk and the hoopoe flew until they came to Sulayman, who was sitting on his throne. The hawk said: "I have brought him to you, O prophet of God."

When the hoopoe came near him, it raised its head, let down its tail and wings, dragging them on the ground in humility before Sulayman. When it drew close to him, he seized its head, pulled it towards him and said: "Where have you been? I will surely punish you with a severe punishment." The hoopoe said to him: "O prophet of God, remember your standing before God, glorified is He." When Sulayman heard that, he trembled and pardoned it.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed me, saying: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Rijal narrated to us in Baghdad, saying: Ibrahim ibn Bistam narrated to us from Abu Qutaybah, from al-Hasan ibn Abi Ja'far al-Ja'fari, from al-Zubayr ibn Hurayth, from 'Ikrimah, who said: "Sulayman (peace be upon him) was only turned away from slaughtering the hoopoe because of his kindness to his parents."

They said: Then he asked it, saying: "What has delayed you from me?" The hoopoe said: "What God has informed of in His saying: [fa-makatha ghayra ba'id] (and it tarried not long)." The common reading is with a dammah on the kaf, while 'Asim, Ya'qub and Abu Hatim read it with a fathah, and both are well-known dialects.

[fa-qala ahatu bima lam tuhit bihi] (He said: "I have encompassed what you have not encompassed") means: I know what you do not know. [wa-ji'tuka min Saba'] (and I have come to you from Saba'). Al-Hasan, Abu 'Amr, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Humayd and Ibn Kathir, in the narration of al-Bazzi, read min Saba'a, with both hamzas open and without tanwin, treating it as the name of a tribe; this is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd. The rest read it in the genitive (min Saba'in), taking it as the name of a man. The report also states that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about Saba', and he said: "He was a man who had ten sons; six of them were on the right and four on the left." We will mention their names and their story in Surat Saba', God willing, the Mighty and Majestic. And the poet said:

"The Wariddun and Taym are at the peaks of Saba,
the buffalo hide has bitten their necks."

[bi-naba'in yaqin] (with certain news): with news that there is no doubt in.

Wahb said: The hoopoe said: "I have found a king whom your kingdom has not reached."

[Inni wajadtu imra'atan tamlikuhum] (Indeed I found a woman ruling them). Her name was Bilqis, daughter of al-Sharah, who is al-Hudhadh. It was said: Sharahil ibn Dhi Hadan ibn al-Yashrij ibn al-Harith ibn Qays ibn Sufa ibn Saba ibn Yashkhub ibn Ya'rub ibn Qahtan. Bilqis's father, who was called al-Yashrij and nicknamed al-Hudhadh, was a king of great station; forty kings were born to him, and he ruled all the land of Yemen. He used to say to the kings of the outlying regions: "None of you is my equal." He refused to marry among them, so they married him to a woman from the jinn called Rayhana, daughter of al-Sakan, and she bore him Tilmaqa, who is Bilqis; he had no child other than her.

This is confirmed by what:

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hurim ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Qatadah, from al-Nadr ibn Anas, from Bishr ibn Nahik, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "One of Bilqis's two parents was a jinn."

They said: When the father of Bilqis died, leaving no child other than her, she coveted the kingdom and asked her people to pledge allegiance to her. Some obeyed her and others disobeyed her, so they chose a man over her and made him king over them. They split into two factions, each faction taking control of a region of the land of Yemen with its kingdom.

Then this man whom they had made king behaved badly towards the people of his kingdom, to the point that he would reach out his hand to the women of his subjects and commit fornication with them. His companions wanted to depose him, but they could not overpower him. When Bilqis saw that, jealousy seized her, and she sent to him offering herself to him. The king replied: "By God, what prevented me from beginning with a proposal to you was only my despair of you." She said: "I am not averse to you, for you are a noble match. Gather the men of my people and propose to me before them." He gathered them and proposed to her before them. They said: "We do not think she will do this." He said to them: "Rather, it is she who initiated with me, so I want you to hear her words and bear witness against her." When they came to her and mentioned that to her, she said: "Yes, I wanted a husband and I never ceased to; I was averse to this before, but now I am content with him, so marry me to him." When she was conducted to him, she went out with many people of her servants and retinue, until his residences and houses were filled with them. When she came to him, she gave him wine until he became drunk, then she cut off his head and returned at night to her dwelling. When the people awoke, they saw the king slain with his head set up at the gate of her house, and they knew that that marriage had been deceit and treachery on her part. They gathered to her and said: "You are more worthy of this kingdom than anyone else." She said: "Had it not been for shame and disgrace, I would not have killed him, but his corruption had spread, and zeal seized me until I did what I did." So they made her queen, and her affair was established.[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/211, with variations.]] [110]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Khadijah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi al-Layth narrated to us in Baghdad, saying: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Muslim, from al-Hasan, from Abu Bakrah, who said: Bilqis was mentioned in the presence of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "A people who entrust their affairs to a woman will never prosper."[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/211.]] [111]

[Wa-utiyat min kulli shay'] (And she had been given of everything): of what kings need in terms of equipment and provisions.

[Wa-laha 'arshun 'azim] (And she has a mighty throne): a huge, fine throne. Its front was of gold inlaid with red rubies and green emeralds, and its back was of silver adorned with various kinds of jewels. It had four legs: one of red ruby, one of emerald, one of green ruby, and one of pearl; the panels of the throne were of gold, and upon it were seven doors, each chamber having a closed door.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Bilqis's throne was thirty cubits by thirty cubits, and its height in the air was thirty cubits.

Muqatil said: It was eighty cubits by thirty cubits, and its height in the air was eighty cubits, adorned with jewels.

[Wajadtuha wa-qawmaha yasjudna lil-shams min duni Allah] (I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of God), [wa-zayyana lahumu al-shaytanu a'malahum fa-sadahum 'ani al-sabili fa-hum la yahtadun] (and Satan adorned for them their deeds and barred them from the path, so they are not guided), [alla yasjudu lillah] (that they should not prostrate to God). Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Balkhi, al-Hasan, Abu Ja'far, Humayd, al-A'raj, al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub, in the narration of Ruways, read "ala usjudu" with a light (takhfif) pronunciation, in the sense of: "Ala, O people, prostrate!", taking it as a command from God, the Exalted, begun anew, and omitting "ya ha'ula'" (O you people) as indicated by its agent. Some have cited from the Arabs by report: "Ala ya arhamuna" (Ah, O have mercy on us!), "Ala ya tasaddaqu 'alayna" (Ah, O give alms to us!), meaning "Ala ya qawm" (O people), like the saying of al-Akhtal:

"Ala ya Salma, ya Hind, Hind of the Banu Badr,
even if our neighbour has passed away, it is forever."

According to this reading, "usjudu" is in the jussive position as a command, and one pauses on "ala," then begins "usjudu."

Al-Farra' said: Al-Kisa'i narrated to me from 'Isa al-Hamadhani, who said: I never heard the shaykhs reading it except with light pronunciation, intending the imperative. It appears in the reading of 'Abd Allah as "hal-la tasjudu lillah" with the ta', and in the reading of Ubayy as "ala yasjudna lillah." These two readings are proof for those who read it lightly. The rest read "alla yasjudu" with emphasis (tashdid), meaning: [wa-zayyana lahumu al-shaytanu a'malahum] (Satan adorned for them their deeds) so that they would not prostrate to God. "Allā" is in the accusative position, and "yasjudu" is in the accusative by "an." Abu 'Ubayd chose this reading and said: "The light pronunciation has a good aspect, but in it the report is cut off from the matter of Saba' and its people, and then it returns after to mention them; whereas the reading with emphasis is a continuous report, one part following another, with no break in its middle. The pause is on 'ala' and then one begins 'yasjudu,' just as one connects [alladhi yukhriju al-khab'a]."

[Alladhi yukhriju al-khab'a fi al-samawati wal-ard] (He who brings forth the hidden in the heavens and the earth): meaning the unseen of the heavens and the earth.

Most exegetes said: the hidden of the heaven is rain, and the hidden of the earth is plants. In the reading of 'Abd Allah: "yukhriju al-khab'a min al-samawat," and "min" and "fi" are interchangeable. The Arabs say: "La-astakhrijanna al-'ilma fikum," meaning "minkum" (from you). This is related by al-Farra'.

[Wa-ya'lamu ma yukhfuna wa-ma yu'linun] (And He knows what they conceal and what they proclaim): the common reading has the verbs with "ya" in both, while al-Kisa'i read them with "ta," and this is the narration of Hafs from 'Asim.

[Allahu la ilaha illa huwa rabbu al-'arshi al-'azim] (God—there is no god but He, Lord of the Mighty Throne): the throne, however great it is, is inferior to Him; no throne resembles Him, neither the throne of the queen of Saba' nor any other.

Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Zayd said: From His saying [ahatu bima lam tuhit bihi] up to His saying [la ilaha illa huwa rabbu al-'arshi al-'azim], the whole is the speech of the hoopoe.

And We gave David and Solomon knowledge, and they said, "Praise be to God, who has favoured us above many of His believing servants." ﴿And Solomon inherited David.﴾ He inherited his prophethood, his knowledge and his kingship, to the exclusion of David's other sons, and David had nineteen sons.

Muqatil said: Solomon had greater kingship than David and was more judicious than him, while David was more devoted in worship than Solomon (peace be upon them both).

﴿And Solomon said,﴾ giving thanks for the blessings of God, the Glorified and Exalted, upon him: "O people, we have been taught the speech of the birds," meaning that God made their speech like the speech of the children of Adam, since he understood it from them, "and we have been given of everything. Indeed, this is evidently a great favour."

Muqatil said concerning this verse: Solomon (peace be upon him) was sitting when a bird flew past him. He said to his companions, "Do you know what the bird that passed by us is saying?" They said, "You know best." Solomon said, "It said to me:

'Peace be upon you, O king who holds power over the Children of Israel. May God, the Glorified and Exalted, grant you honour and give you victory over your enemy. I am going to my young, and then I will pass by you again.'

And it will return to us a second time, so watch its return."

He said: The people looked for a long time, and then it passed by them and said, "Peace be upon you, O king. If you will permit me, I will gather food for my young until they grow up, and then I will come to you, and do with me what you wish." Solomon informed them of what it had said, and he gave it permission.

Farqad al-Sakhi said: Solomon passed by a nightingale on a tree, moving its head and tilting its tail. He said to his companions, "Do you know what this nightingale is saying?" They said, "God and His Prophet know best." He said, "It is saying: 'I ate half a date, so let the world be forgotten.'"

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-'Adl informed me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanbah and Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan narrated to us, both saying: al-Fadl ibn al-'Abbas al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying:

Musa ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: 'Abbad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from al-Kalbi, from a man, from Ka'b, who said:

A turtledove cried out in the presence of Solomon ibn Dawud (peace be upon him), and he said, "Do you know what it is saying?"
They said, "No."
He said, "It is saying: [[In the second manuscript (Isfahan) there is an addition: 'Build for death and construct for ruin.' A dove cried out in the presence of Solomon, and he said: "Do you know what it is saying?" They said, "No." He said, "It is saying:"]] 'Would that these creatures had not been created.'"

A peacock cried out in the presence of Solomon (peace be upon him), and he said, "Do you know what it is saying?"
They said, "No."
He said, "It is saying [[In the second manuscript there is an addition: 'As you judge, so you will be judged.' A hoopoe cried out in the presence of Solomon, and he said: "Do you know what it is saying?" They said, "No." He said, "It is saying:"]] 'Whoever does not show mercy will not be shown mercy.'"

A sparrow-hawk (sard) cried out in the presence of Solomon, and he said, "Do you know what it is saying?"
They said, "No."
He said, "It is saying: 'Seek forgiveness from God, O sinners.' For this reason the Messenger of God (ﷺ) forbade killing it."

Then a tuttuwa (a small bird) cried out in the presence of Solomon (peace be upon him), and he said, "Do you know what it is saying?"
They said, "No."
He said, "It is saying: 'Every living thing will die, and every new thing will decay.'"

A swallow cried out in the presence of Solomon (peace be upon him), and he said, "Do you know what it is saying?"
They said, "No."
He said, "It is saying: 'Send forward good, and you will find it.' For this reason the Messenger of God (ﷺ) forbade killing it."

A dove cooed in the presence of Solomon (peace be upon him), and he said, "Do you know what this dove is saying?" They said, "No."
He said, "It is saying: 'Glory be to my Lord, the Most High, whose heaven and earth are full of Him.'"

A Qumri (a type of dove) cried out in the presence of Solomon (peace be upon him), and he said, "Do you know what it is saying?"
They said, "No."
He said, "It is saying: 'Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.' The raven calls down curses upon the tax collector. The kite says: 'Everything perishes except God.' The sand partridge says: 'Whoever keeps silent is safe.' The parrot says: 'Woe to him whose concern is the world.' The frog says: 'Glory be to my Lord, the Holy.' The falcon says: 'Glory be to my Lord and praise be to Him.' The female frog says: 'Glory be to the One who is remembered in every place.'"

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan narrated to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn al-'Abbas ibn Mihran narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Isma'il informed us, from 'Ayyash, from Zirr, from Makhul, who said: A partridge cried out in the presence of Solomon ibn Dawud (peace be upon him), and he said, "Do you know what it is saying?"
They said, "No."
He said, "It is saying: 'The Most Merciful settled Himself upon the Throne.'"

And with its chain from Musa ibn Ibrahim, who said: Salih al-Harawi informed us, from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When the rooster crows, it is saying: 'Remember God, O heedless ones.'" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/166.]] [108]

Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, who said: When the vulture cries out, it says: "O son of Adam, live as you wish, its end is death." When the eagle cries out, it says: "In distance from people is companionship." When the qabbar (a type of bird) cries out, it says: "My God, curse those who hate the family of Muhammad." When the swallow cries out, it recites: ﴿Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds﴾, prolonging the "ḍāllīn" (the final word, "those who go astray") as a reciter would prolong it.

﴿And for Solomon were gathered his armies of jinn and humans and birds, and they were marshalled in ranks.﴾ That is, they were gathered and assembled for him on a march, "so they were kept in order," meaning that the first of them was held back until the last of them had gathered. This was because he placed over each category of them guards (wuzʿah) who restrained the front of them until the rear caught up, so that they would not advance ahead in the march, as kings do.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "yūza'ūn" means "they are pushed back." Ibn Zayd and Muqatil said: "They are driven." Al-Suddi said: "They are made to stop." The root of wazʿ in the Arabic language is restraint and prevention, and from it comes the hadith: "The ruler restrains more than the Qur'an restrains." It is also said, "awza'ahu al-amr," meaning he charged him with the matter.

In a report: "People must have guards (wuzʿah)." And a poet said:

"When I rebuked the greying hair for my youth, and said: 'Would that I were sound, but the greying hair is a restrainer.'" [[Lisan al-'Arab: 4/83.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Talhah ibn Muhammad and 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad narrated to us, both saying: Abu Bakr ibn Mujahid narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sunayd narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Abu Ma'shar, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, concerning this verse, who said: It has reached us that Solomon's army was a hundred farsakhs (a unit of distance): twenty-five of them were for humans, twenty-five for jinn, twenty-five for wild animals, and twenty-five for birds. He had a thousand tents of glass upon wooden frames, in which were three hundred wives and seven hundred concubines. He commanded the violent wind, and it carried him, and he commanded the gentle wind, and it moved him along. It was revealed to him, while he was travelling between heaven and earth: "I have increased your kingdom: no creature will speak a word, but the wind will come and inform you of it."

Muqatil said: The devils wove for Solomon (peace be upon him) a carpet one farsakh by one farsakh, of gold woven into silk. A golden pulpit was placed for him in the middle of the carpet, and he sat upon it, and around him were three thousand thrones of gold and silver. The prophets sat on golden thrones, the scholars on silver thrones, and the people surrounded them, and around the people were the jinn and the devils. The birds shaded him with their wings so that the sun would not fall upon him, and the east wind lifted the carpet, travelling a month's distance from morning to afternoon and from afternoon to morning.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Malik al-Qati'i narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ayyub narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr, that is Ibn 'Ayyash, narrated to us, from Idris ibn Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: My father told me that Solomon (peace be upon him) once rode the sea. He passed by a farmer, who looked at him and said: "The family of David has been given a great kingdom." The wind carried his words to Solomon's ear, so he descended and came to the farmer and said: "I have heard your words, and I came to you only so that you would not wish for what you cannot attain. One single glorification that God, the Exalted, accepts is better than what the family of David has been given." The farmer said: "May God remove your worry as you have removed mine."

﴿Until, when they came upon the valley of the ants.﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Makhlad ibn Ja'far [[In the second manuscript there is an addition: al-Baqawi.]] narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Alawiyyah narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn 'Isa narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Abu Ilyas informed us, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, from Ka'b, who said: When Solomon (peace be upon him) rode, he carried his family and all his retinue, his servants and scribes, in those canopies one above another according to their ranks. He had kitchens and bakeries carried with him, with iron ovens and large cooking pots, each capable of holding the contents of ten slaughtered camels. He had arenas for the animals set out in front of him. Cooks cooked, bakers baked, and the animals ran before him between heaven and earth, while the wind swept them along.

He travelled with those who accompanied him toward Yemen, and he took the route through Madinah, the city of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Solomon said: "This is the abode of emigration of a prophet at the end of time. Blessed is whoever believes in him, blessed is whoever follows him, and blessed is whoever takes him as a model." He saw around the House (the Ka'bah) idols being worshipped apart from God, the Glorified. When Solomon passed by the House, the House wept. God, the Glorified, revealed to the House: "What makes you weep?" It said: "My Lord, a prophet of Yours and a people of Your friends passed by me, but they did not descend in me, they did not pray at me, and they did not mention You in my presence, while idols are worshipped around me apart from You." God, the Glorified, revealed to it: "Do not weep, for I will fill you with prostrating faces, and I will send down in you a new Qur'an, and I will raise up from you a prophet at the end of time, the most beloved of My prophets to Me. I will place in you people from My creation who will worship Me, and I will prescribe for My servants an obligation, so that they will hasten to you as eagles hasten to their nests, and yearn for you as a she-camel yearns for her young and a dove for her egg. I will purify you from idols and the worshippers of Satan."

He said: Then Solomon proceeded until he passed through the Valley of Sadir, a valley of al-Ta'if. He came upon the valley of the ants, and a single ant was walking, and it was lame, limping, and it was as large as a male... in size. The ant called out: ﴿O ants, enter your dwellings, lest Solomon and his armies crush you without their perceiving it.﴾ This means that Solomon understood its speech, and no creature spoke except that the wind carried it and cast it into the ears of Solomon (peace be upon him).

He said: ﴿So he smiled, laughing at its speech, and said: "My Lord, grant me the ability to be grateful for Your blessing..." up to His words: "among Your righteous servants."﴾ That is, "among Your monotheist servants."

Qatadah and Muqatil said: The valley of the ants was in the land of Syria.

Nawf al-Himyari said: The ants of the valley of Solomon were like flies.

al-Sha'bi said: The ant whose speech Solomon understood had two wings.

Muqatil said: Solomon heard its speech from three miles away. They differed about the name of that ant.

Abu 'Abd Allah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Husayni al-Dinawari informed me, saying: Abu al-'Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Sarsari narrated to us, saying: al-Haytham ibn Khalaf al-Duri narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn Hatim al-Bazzaz narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Zabarqan al-Taymi narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, who said: The name of the ant that spoke to Solomon ibn Dawud (peace be upon him) was Tahiyah.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Talhah and 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Mujahid narrated to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abu Muhammad al-Nu'man ibn Shibl al-Bahili narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Rawq narrated to us, from his father, who said: The name of Solomon's ant was Harami, and this is the saying of Muqatil.

I saw in some books that when Solomon heard the speech of the ant, he said: "Bring her to me." They brought her to him, and he said to her: "Why did you warn the ants against my injustice? Do you not know that I am a just prophet? Why did you say: 'Lest Solomon and his armies crush you'?" The ant said: "Did you not hear my words: 'without their perceiving it'? Moreover, I did not intend the crushing of souls, but the crushing of hearts. I feared that they would long for what you have been given and would occupy themselves with looking rather than with glorification." He said to her: "Advise me." The ant said: "Do you know why your father was named David?" He said: "No." She said: "Because he treated his wound and it healed." "Do you know why you were named Solomon?" He said: "No." She said: "Because you are sound (salim), and you were given what you were given because of the soundness of your heart, and you are destined to join your father." Then she said: "Do you know why God subjected the wind to you?" He said: "No." She said: "God has informed you that the whole world is wind." So Solomon smiled, laughing in wonder at her speech, and said: "My Lord, grant me the ability..." to the end of the verse.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah informed us, saying: al-Hadrami informed us, saying: Hasan al-Khallal narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) forbade the killing of four kinds of animals: the hoopoe, the sparrow-hawk, the bee, and the ant.

﴿And he inspected the birds﴾, that is, he sought them and searched for them. ﴿And said: "Why do I not see the hoopoe? Or is it among the absent?"﴾ Ibn Kathir, 'Asim, al-Kisa'i and Ayyub read the (lī, "to me") here and in Surat Ya-Sin, "wa mā lī lā a'budu" [[Surat Ya-Sin: 22.]]. Hamzah read the yā' in both places (as a lengthened vowel). As for Abu 'Amr, he read the yā' in this place but read it with a fatḥah in Ya-Sin, and he distinguished between them, saying: "Because the one here is a question, and the other is a negation."

"Am" (or) here: it is said the mīm is an added particle. It is also said that "am" here means "bal" (rather), so the meaning is "rather, was he among the absent?"

﴿I will surely punish him with a severe punishment.﴾ His punishment would be that his feathers and tail be plucked out, leaving him bare, and then he would be thrown into an ant-hill so that the ants would bite him. 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad said: "Plucking and exposing him to the sun."
al-Dahhak: "I will tie his leg tightly and expose him to the sun."
Muqatil ibn Hayyan: "I will coat him with tar and expose him to the sun."
It is also said: "I will confine him in a cage." It is also said: "I will separate him from his mate." It is also said: "I will prevent him from serving me." It is also said: "I will scatter him."

﴿Or I will slaughter him, or he will bring me a clear authority.﴾ That is, a manifest proof.

As for the reason for Solomon's searching for the hoopoe and asking about it among the birds, it was that it neglected the turn of duty it was assigned, and Solomon (peace be upon him) needed water. He did not know where the water was. It was said to him: "The knowledge of that is with the hoopoe." He searched for it, did not find it, and threatened it. The story concerning it, as the scholars of the lives of the prophets have related, has intermingled accounts of some with others:

When the Prophet of God, Solomon (ﷺ), finished building the Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), he resolved to set out for the land of the Haram. He prepared for the journey and took with him humans, jinn, devils, birds and wild animals, until his army reached a hundred farsakhs. He commanded the gentle wind, and it carried them. When he arrived at the Haram and remained there as long as God willed him to remain, he slaughtered each day, during his stay, a total of five thousand camels, five thousand bulls and twenty thousand sheep.

He said to the notables of his people who were present: "This is a place from which a prophet of Arab origin will come forth, whose description is such and such. He will be given victory over all who oppose him, and his awe will reach a distance of a month's journey, the near and the far being equal in his sight in truth, and he will not be deterred by the blame of any blamer concerning God."

They said: "Then which religion shall we follow, O Prophet of God?" He said: "The religion of the Hanifiyyah (the pure monotheism of Abraham). Blessed is whoever reaches him, believes in him and affirms him."

They said: "How far is it between us and his coming forth, O Prophet of God?" He said: "About a thousand years. Let the present among you inform the absent, for he is the master of the prophets and the seal of the messengers, and his name is Muhammad among the company of the prophets."

He remained in Mecca until he had completed his rites. Then he wished to go to the land of Yemen. He left Mecca in the morning and travelled toward Yemen on the day the star Suhayl rose. He reached Sana'a at midday, and that was a month's journey. He saw a land whose greenness was flourishing, and he wished to alight there to pray and to take his midday meal. They sought water and did not find any, and the hoopoe was his guide to water. It could see the water beneath the earth as one of you sees his cup in his hand. It would peck the earth and know the place of the water and its depth, and then the devils would come and dig it out as a skin is flayed, and then they would extract the water.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Ibn 'Abbas mentioned this report, and Nafi' ibn al-Azraq said to him: "You claim that the hoopoe pecks the earth and sees the water. How can it see this and not see the two grains of wheat that fall around its neck?"

Ibn 'Abbas said to him: "Woe to you! When destiny comes, it intervenes between the sight and what it sees."

Qatadah narrated from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Do not kill the hoopoe, for it was Solomon's guide to the nearness and distance of water, and it loved that God be worshipped on the earth, as it said: ﴿And I have come to you from Saba' with certain news. Indeed, I found a woman...﴾" the verse.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 27, verse 15–26 (part 2 of 2):

They said: When Sulayman descended, the hoopoe said: "Sulayman has become occupied with descending, so ascend towards the sky and look at the length and breadth of the world." So he did that, and he looked to the right and to the left, and he saw a garden and inclined towards the greenery and landed in it. Suddenly he found a hoopoe, and he descended upon it. The name of the hoopoe of Sulayman ibn Dawud (peace be upon him) was Ya'fur, and the name of the hoopoe of Yemen was 'Anfar [[It is also narrated: 'Anfir and 'Anqar.]]. So 'Anfar said to Ya'fur, the hoopoe of Sulayman: "From where have you come, and where are you heading?"

He said: "I have come from al-Sham with my master Sulayman ibn Dawud (peace be upon him)."

The hoopoe said: "And who is Sulayman ibn Dawud?" He said: "The king of the jinn, the humans, the devils, the birds, the beasts and the wind. So where are you from?" He said: "I am from these lands." He said: "And who rules them?" He said: "A woman called Bilqis. Your master Sulayman has a great kingdom, but the kingdom of Bilqis is not inferior to it. She has taken possession of the whole sun, and under her hands are twelve thousand commanders, and under the hand of each commander are a hundred thousand fighters."

"Will you go with me so that you may see her kingdom?" He said: "I fear that Sulayman will look for me at the time of prayer when I need water."

The Yemeni hoopoe said: "Your master would be glad that you bring him news of this queen." So he set out with him, and he looked at Bilqis and her kingdom, and he did not return to Sulayman except at the time of 'Asr.

He said: When Sulayman descended and entered upon his place at the time of prayer, he sought the hoopoe, for he had landed in a place without water. He asked the humans about water, and they said: "We know of no water here." He asked the jinn and the devils, and they did not know either. Then he searched for the hoopoe and did not find it. Ibn 'Abbas said, in some narrations: and he became weary from searching the sun [for it]. Sulayman looked, and saw that the place of the hoopoe was empty. So he called the chief of the birds, who is the eagle (al-nasr), and asked him about the hoopoe. He said: "May God set the king right, I do not know where it is, and I have not sent it to any place." At that, Sulayman (peace be upon him) became angry and said: "I will surely punish it with a severe punishment, or I will surely slaughter it, or it shall bring me a clear authority."

'Ikrimah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Every 'sultan' in the Qur'an means proof."

They said: Then he called the hawk, the lord of the birds, and said: "Bring me the hoopoe at once." So the hawk raised itself above the sky until it settled in the air, and it looked at the world like a bowl before one of you, then it turned to the right and to the left, and suddenly it saw the hoopoe approaching from the direction of Yemen. The hawk swooped down towards it, intending it. When the hoopoe saw that, it knew that the hawk was aiming at it with harm, so it implored it, saying: "By the right of God who gave you strength and empowered you over me, have mercy on me and do not harm me."

So the hawk turned away from it and said to it: "Woe to you, may your mother be bereaved! The prophet of God has sworn that he will punish you or slaughter you." Then they both flew towards Sulayman. When it reached the army, the eagle and the birds met it and said to it: "Woe to you! Where were you absent in this sleep of yours? The prophet of God has threatened you, and they informed him of what he had said."

The hoopoe said: "Did the Messenger of God not make an exception?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Or he shall bring me a clear excuse." Then the hawk and the hoopoe flew until they came to Sulayman, who was sitting on his throne. The hawk said: "I have brought him to you, O prophet of God."

When the hoopoe came near him, it raised its head, let down its tail and wings, dragging them on the ground in humility before Sulayman. When it drew close to him, he seized its head, pulled it towards him and said: "Where have you been? I will surely punish you with a severe punishment." The hoopoe said to him: "O prophet of God, remember your standing before God, glorified is He." When Sulayman heard that, he trembled and pardoned it.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed me, saying: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Rijal narrated to us in Baghdad, saying: Ibrahim ibn Bistam narrated to us from Abu Qutaybah, from al-Hasan ibn Abi Ja'far al-Ja'fari, from al-Zubayr ibn Hurayth, from 'Ikrimah, who said: "Sulayman (peace be upon him) was only turned away from slaughtering the hoopoe because of his kindness to his parents."

They said: Then he asked it, saying: "What has delayed you from me?" The hoopoe said: "What God has informed of in His saying: [fa-makatha ghayra ba'id] (and it tarried not long)." The common reading is with a dammah on the kaf, while 'Asim, Ya'qub and Abu Hatim read it with a fathah, and both are well-known dialects.

[fa-qala ahatu bima lam tuhit bihi] (He said: "I have encompassed what you have not encompassed") means: I know what you do not know. [wa-ji'tuka min Saba'] (and I have come to you from Saba'). Al-Hasan, Abu 'Amr, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Humayd and Ibn Kathir, in the narration of al-Bazzi, read min Saba'a, with both hamzas open and without tanwin, treating it as the name of a tribe; this is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd. The rest read it in the genitive (min Saba'in), taking it as the name of a man. The report also states that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about Saba', and he said: "He was a man who had ten sons; six of them were on the right and four on the left." We will mention their names and their story in Surat Saba', God willing, the Mighty and Majestic. And the poet said:

"The Wariddun and Taym are at the peaks of Saba,
the buffalo hide has bitten their necks."

[bi-naba'in yaqin] (with certain news): with news that there is no doubt in.

Wahb said: The hoopoe said: "I have found a king whom your kingdom has not reached."

[Inni wajadtu imra'atan tamlikuhum] (Indeed I found a woman ruling them). Her name was Bilqis, daughter of al-Sharah, who is al-Hudhadh. It was said: Sharahil ibn Dhi Hadan ibn al-Yashrij ibn al-Harith ibn Qays ibn Sufa ibn Saba ibn Yashkhub ibn Ya'rub ibn Qahtan. Bilqis's father, who was called al-Yashrij and nicknamed al-Hudhadh, was a king of great station; forty kings were born to him, and he ruled all the land of Yemen. He used to say to the kings of the outlying regions: "None of you is my equal." He refused to marry among them, so they married him to a woman from the jinn called Rayhana, daughter of al-Sakan, and she bore him Tilmaqa, who is Bilqis; he had no child other than her.

This is confirmed by what:

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hurim ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Qatadah, from al-Nadr ibn Anas, from Bishr ibn Nahik, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "One of Bilqis's two parents was a jinn."

They said: When the father of Bilqis died, leaving no child other than her, she coveted the kingdom and asked her people to pledge allegiance to her. Some obeyed her and others disobeyed her, so they chose a man over her and made him king over them. They split into two factions, each faction taking control of a region of the land of Yemen with its kingdom.

Then this man whom they had made king behaved badly towards the people of his kingdom, to the point that he would reach out his hand to the women of his subjects and commit fornication with them. His companions wanted to depose him, but they could not overpower him. When Bilqis saw that, jealousy seized her, and she sent to him offering herself to him. The king replied: "By God, what prevented me from beginning with a proposal to you was only my despair of you." She said: "I am not averse to you, for you are a noble match. Gather the men of my people and propose to me before them." He gathered them and proposed to her before them. They said: "We do not think she will do this." He said to them: "Rather, it is she who initiated with me, so I want you to hear her words and bear witness against her." When they came to her and mentioned that to her, she said: "Yes, I wanted a husband and I never ceased to; I was averse to this before, but now I am content with him, so marry me to him." When she was conducted to him, she went out with many people of her servants and retinue, until his residences and houses were filled with them. When she came to him, she gave him wine until he became drunk, then she cut off his head and returned at night to her dwelling. When the people awoke, they saw the king slain with his head set up at the gate of her house, and they knew that that marriage had been deceit and treachery on her part. They gathered to her and said: "You are more worthy of this kingdom than anyone else." She said: "Had it not been for shame and disgrace, I would not have killed him, but his corruption had spread, and zeal seized me until I did what I did." So they made her queen, and her affair was established.[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/211, with variations.]] [110]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Khadijah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi al-Layth narrated to us in Baghdad, saying: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Muslim, from al-Hasan, from Abu Bakrah, who said: Bilqis was mentioned in the presence of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "A people who entrust their affairs to a woman will never prosper."[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/211.]] [111]

[Wa-utiyat min kulli shay'] (And she had been given of everything): of what kings need in terms of equipment and provisions.

[Wa-laha 'arshun 'azim] (And she has a mighty throne): a huge, fine throne. Its front was of gold inlaid with red rubies and green emeralds, and its back was of silver adorned with various kinds of jewels. It had four legs: one of red ruby, one of emerald, one of green ruby, and one of pearl; the panels of the throne were of gold, and upon it were seven doors, each chamber having a closed door.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Bilqis's throne was thirty cubits by thirty cubits, and its height in the air was thirty cubits.

Muqatil said: It was eighty cubits by thirty cubits, and its height in the air was eighty cubits, adorned with jewels.

[Wajadtuha wa-qawmaha yasjudna lil-shams min duni Allah] (I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of God), [wa-zayyana lahumu al-shaytanu a'malahum fa-sadahum 'ani al-sabili fa-hum la yahtadun] (and Satan adorned for them their deeds and barred them from the path, so they are not guided), [alla yasjudu lillah] (that they should not prostrate to God). Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Balkhi, al-Hasan, Abu Ja'far, Humayd, al-A'raj, al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub, in the narration of Ruways, read "ala usjudu" with a light (takhfif) pronunciation, in the sense of: "Ala, O people, prostrate!", taking it as a command from God, the Exalted, begun anew, and omitting "ya ha'ula'" (O you people) as indicated by its agent. Some have cited from the Arabs by report: "Ala ya arhamuna" (Ah, O have mercy on us!), "Ala ya tasaddaqu 'alayna" (Ah, O give alms to us!), meaning "Ala ya qawm" (O people), like the saying of al-Akhtal:

"Ala ya Salma, ya Hind, Hind of the Banu Badr,
even if our neighbour has passed away, it is forever."

According to this reading, "usjudu" is in the jussive position as a command, and one pauses on "ala," then begins "usjudu."

Al-Farra' said: Al-Kisa'i narrated to me from 'Isa al-Hamadhani, who said: I never heard the shaykhs reading it except with light pronunciation, intending the imperative. It appears in the reading of 'Abd Allah as "hal-la tasjudu lillah" with the ta', and in the reading of Ubayy as "ala yasjudna lillah." These two readings are proof for those who read it lightly. The rest read "alla yasjudu" with emphasis (tashdid), meaning: [wa-zayyana lahumu al-shaytanu a'malahum] (Satan adorned for them their deeds) so that they would not prostrate to God. "Allā" is in the accusative position, and "yasjudu" is in the accusative by "an." Abu 'Ubayd chose this reading and said: "The light pronunciation has a good aspect, but in it the report is cut off from the matter of Saba' and its people, and then it returns after to mention them; whereas the reading with emphasis is a continuous report, one part following another, with no break in its middle. The pause is on 'ala' and then one begins 'yasjudu,' just as one connects [alladhi yukhriju al-khab'a]."

[Alladhi yukhriju al-khab'a fi al-samawati wal-ard] (He who brings forth the hidden in the heavens and the earth): meaning the unseen of the heavens and the earth.

Most exegetes said: the hidden of the heaven is rain, and the hidden of the earth is plants. In the reading of 'Abd Allah: "yukhriju al-khab'a min al-samawat," and "min" and "fi" are interchangeable. The Arabs say: "La-astakhrijanna al-'ilma fikum," meaning "minkum" (from you). This is related by al-Farra'.

[Wa-ya'lamu ma yukhfuna wa-ma yu'linun] (And He knows what they conceal and what they proclaim): the common reading has the verbs with "ya" in both, while al-Kisa'i read them with "ta," and this is the narration of Hafs from 'Asim.

[Allahu la ilaha illa huwa rabbu al-'arshi al-'azim] (God—there is no god but He, Lord of the Mighty Throne): the throne, however great it is, is inferior to Him; no throne resembles Him, neither the throne of the queen of Saba' nor any other.

Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Zayd said: From His saying [ahatu bima lam tuhit bihi] up to His saying [la ilaha illa huwa rabbu al-'arshi al-'azim], the whole is the speech of the hoopoe.

And We gave David and Solomon knowledge, and they said, "Praise be to God, who has favoured us above many of His believing servants." ﴿And Solomon inherited David.﴾ He inherited his prophethood, his knowledge and his kingship, to the exclusion of David's other sons, and David had nineteen sons.

Muqatil said: Solomon had greater kingship than David and was more judicious than him, while David was more devoted in worship than Solomon (peace be upon them both).

﴿And Solomon said,﴾ giving thanks for the blessings of God, the Glorified and Exalted, upon him: "O people, we have been taught the speech of the birds," meaning that God made their speech like the speech of the children of Adam, since he understood it from them, "and we have been given of everything. Indeed, this is evidently a great favour."

Muqatil said concerning this verse: Solomon (peace be upon him) was sitting when a bird flew past him. He said to his companions, "Do you know what the bird that passed by us is saying?" They said, "You know best." Solomon said, "It said to me:

'Peace be upon you, O king who holds power over the Children of Israel. May God, the Glorified and Exalted, grant you honour and give you victory over your enemy. I am going to my young, and then I will pass by you again.'

And it will return to us a second time, so watch its return."

He said: The people looked for a long time, and then it passed by them and said, "Peace be upon you, O king. If you will permit me, I will gather food for my young until they grow up, and then I will come to you, and do with me what you wish." Solomon informed them of what it had said, and he gave it permission.

Farqad al-Sakhi said: Solomon passed by a nightingale on a tree, moving its head and tilting its tail. He said to his companions, "Do you know what this nightingale is saying?" They said, "God and His Prophet know best." He said, "It is saying: 'I ate half a date, so let the world be forgotten.'"

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-'Adl informed me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanbah and Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan narrated to us, both saying: al-Fadl ibn al-'Abbas al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying:

Musa ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: 'Abbad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from al-Kalbi, from a man, from Ka'b, who said:

A turtledove cried out in the presence of Solomon ibn Dawud (peace be upon him), and he said, "Do you know what it is saying?"
They said, "No."
He said, "It is saying: [[In the second manuscript (Isfahan) there is an addition: 'Build for death and construct for ruin.' A dove cried out in the presence of Solomon, and he said: "Do you know what it is saying?" They said, "No." He said, "It is saying:"]] 'Would that these creatures had not been created.'"

A peacock cried out in the presence of Solomon (peace be upon him), and he said, "Do you know what it is saying?"
They said, "No."
He said, "It is saying [[In the second manuscript there is an addition: 'As you judge, so you will be judged.'
