[[What follows: Tabaqat al-Mufassirin, al-Suyuti, p. 37.]]

"And I am sending them a gift." That is because Bilqis was shrewd, having been tested and having tested others, so she said to the chiefs of her people: "I am sending to Solomon and his people a gift, to win him over with it regarding my kingdom, and to test him with it: is he a king?" If he is a king, he will accept the gift and withdraw; but if he is a prophet, he will not accept the gift, and will not be pleased with anything from us except that we follow his religion. So she sent him a servant boy and servant girls.

Ibn Abbas said: She dressed them in one garment, so that the male could not be distinguished from the female.

Mujahid said: She dressed the boys in the dress of girls and the girls in the dress of boys. They differed on their number: Muqatil said: a hundred male servants and a hundred female servants. Mujahid said: two hundred boys and two hundred girls. Al-Kalbi said: ten boys and ten girls. Wahb and others said: five hundred boys and five hundred girls.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Ibn Hanash told us: Ibn Fanjawayh told us: Salamah told us: 'Abd al-Razzaq told us: Ma'mar informed us, from Thabit al-Bunani, regarding His saying "And I am sending them a gift": She sent him sheets of gold in cases of brocade. When this reached Solomon, he commanded the jinn, who coated the bricks with gold, and then he ordered them cast into the road. When they came, they saw them strewn along the road everywhere. They said: "We have come bearing something, yet here are things lying about which no one even looks at." So what they had brought seemed small in their eyes. It was also said: there were four gold bricks. Wahb and others among the People of the Book said: Bilqis chose five hundred girls and five hundred boys; she dressed the girls in the clothing of boys, the tunics and belts, and dressed the boys in the clothing of girls, and put bracelets of gold on their forearms, and collars of gold around their necks, and earrings and ornaments set with various jewels; she loaded the girls on five hundred mares and the boys on five hundred mules, each horse with a golden bridle set with jewels and covers of coloured brocade. She also sent him five hundred bricks of gold and five hundred bricks of silver, and a crown studded with pearls and rising rubies, and she also sent musk, ambergris, and aloes-wood. She took a casket and placed in it a single unpierced pearl and a bent-holed jewel with a twisted hole, and summoned a man of the nobles of her people called al-Mundhir ibn 'Amr, and attached to him men of her people who were men of opinion and intellect, and she wrote a letter with him, a copy of the gift, and said: "If you are a prophet, distinguish between the male servants and the female servants, tell what is in the casket before you open it, and pierce the pearl with an even hole and thread a string through it." She commanded the boys, saying: "When Solomon speaks to you, speak to him in a manner with feminine softness and effeminacy, resembling women's speech," and she commanded the girls to speak to him in a harsh manner resembling men's speech. Then she said to the messenger: "Look at the man when you enter upon him: if he looks at you with a look of anger, know that he is a king, and let his appearance not overawe you, for I am more honoured than he; but if you see the man cheerful and gentle, know that he is a prophet sent, so understand his words and return the answer."

The messenger set off with the gifts, and the hoopoe came hastening to Solomon (peace be upon him) and informed him of the whole matter. Solomon (peace be upon him) commanded the jinn to strike bricks of gold and silver, and they did so. Then he commanded them to spread out from the place where he was to a distance of nine farsakhs a single courtyard paved with bricks of gold and silver, and to make around the courtyard a wall with battlements of gold and silver, and they did. Then he said: "Which of the animals is finer than what you have seen on land and sea?" They said: "O prophet of Allah, we have seen animals in the sea of such-and-such, striped, separate, of varied colours, having wings, manes and forelocks." He said: "Bring them to me at once," and they were brought. He said: "Tie them on the right side of the courtyard and on its left, upon the bricks of gold and silver, and throw their fodder to them."

Then he said to the jinn: "Bring me your children," and a great multitude gathered; he set them up on the right side of the courtyard and its left. Then Solomon (peace be upon him) sat in his assembly upon his throne, and forty thousand chairs were placed for him on his right and the same number on his left. He commanded the devils to line up in ranks for farsakhs, and commanded mankind to line up for farsakhs, and commanded the wild beasts, the predators, the vermin and the birds to line up for farsakhs on his right and his left.

When the people saw the courtyard and looked at the kingdom of Solomon (peace be upon him), and saw animals whose like their eyes had never seen dunging upon bricks of gold and silver, their souls seemed small to them, and they remained with what they had of gifts.

In some reports, when Solomon (peace be upon him) commanded that the courtyard be paved with bricks of gold and silver, he commanded them to leave on their road a place the size of the bricks they had with them; so when the envoys saw the place of the bricks empty while the whole ground was paved, they feared they would be accused of this, so they threw what they had into that place.

They said: Then they came, and when they saw the devils they looked at a wondrous place and were frightened. The devils said to them: "Pass on, there is no harm upon you." So they kept passing by rank after rank of jinn, mankind, birds, predators and wild beasts, until they stood before Solomon (peace be upon him). Solomon looked at them with a pleasant look and an open face, and said: "What is behind you?" The leader of the people informed him of what they had come for, and gave him the queen's letter. He looked into it and said: "Where is the casket?" It was brought to him, and he shook it. Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him and told him what was in the casket, and he said: "Indeed there is in it a single unpierced pearl and a jewel with a bent hole, twisted in its perforation." The messenger said: "You have spoken truly; so pierce the pearl and thread the string through the jewel." Solomon (peace be upon him) said: "Who will pierce it for me?" He asked mankind, but they had no knowledge of that; then he asked the jinn, and they had no knowledge of that; then he asked the devils, and they said: "Send for the termite." The termite came, took a hair in its mouth and entered the hole, and came out the other side. Solomon (peace be upon him) said to it: "What is your need?" It said: "Make my sustenance in the wood." He said: "That is yours." Then he said: "Who will thread this jewel?" A white worm said: "I will, O messenger of Allah." The worm took the thread in its mouth and entered the hole until it came out the other side. Solomon said: "What is your need?" It said: "Make my sustenance in fruits." He said: "That is yours."

Then he distinguished between the girls and the boys by commanding them to wash their faces and hands. The girl would take the water from the vessel with one hand, then pour it onto the other hand, then strike the face with it; the boy would take it from the vessel and strike his face with it. The girl would pour water over the inner part of her forearm, the boy over the back of the forearm; the girl would pour the water in a pouring stream, and the boy would let the water run down his hand in a trickle. Thus he distinguished between them by that. Then Solomon (peace be upon him) returned the gift.

He said: "Are you supplying me with wealth?" The readers differed concerning it: Hamza and Ya'qub read "atumiddunni" with a single doubled nun, while the others read it with two light nuns and omitted the yā'; Ibn 'Amir, 'Asim, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read with the yā', and the rest with it retained.

"What Allah has given me is better than what He has given you; rather, you rejoice in your gift." That is because you are people of boasting in worldly things and of arrogance through them, and you know nothing else; and this world is not among my needs, for Allah, glorified is He, has empowered me over it and given me in it what He has given no one else, and despite that He has honoured me with religion, prophethood and wisdom. Then he said to al-Mundhir ibn 'Amr, the leader of the delegation: "Return to them with the gift, for we shall certainly come to them with armies they cannot withstand, and we shall certainly expel them from it", i.e., from their land and kingdom, "abased, and they will be humbled" (sāghirūn), i.e., humiliated, if they do not come to me in submission.

Wahb and others among the People of the Book said: When Bilqis's envoys returned to her from Solomon (peace be upon him), she said: "By Allah, I have known that this is no mere king, and we have no power against him, and we can do nothing by rivalling him." She sent to Solomon: "I am coming to you with the kings of my people, so that I may see what your command is and what you call to of your religion." Then she ordered her throne to be placed within seven chambers, one inside another, at the end of the palace, among seven palaces of hers; then she closed the doors behind it and set guards to watch over it. Then she said to the one she left in charge of her realm: "Guard what is before you and my royal throne, so that no one reaches it or adorns it until I come to you." Then she commanded a herald, who proclaimed among the people of her kingdom, informing them of the departure, and she set out toward Solomon with twelve thousand qayls of the kings of Yemen, under each qayl many thousands.

Ibn Abbas said: Solomon was a man of awe who did not begin anything until he was asked about it. One day he went out and sat on his royal throne, and saw a cloud of dust near him, and said: "What is this?"

They said: "Bilqis, O prophet of Allah."

He said: "Has she come down to us to this place?" Ibn Abbas said: The distance between Kufa and al-Hira was about one farsakh. Then Solomon turned to his soldiers and said: "Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?" That is, believers. Ibn Abbas said: obedient.

The scholars differed about the reason for which Solomon (peace be upon him) commanded the bringing of the throne. Most of them said: because Solomon (peace be upon him) knew that if she became Muslim, what was hers would become unlawful to him, so he wished to take her throne before it became unlawful for him to take it by her Islam.

Qatada said: Because its description had pleased him when the hoopoe described it, so he loved to see it.

Ibn Zayd said: He wished to test her intellect, by commanding that it be altered, to see whether she would recognise it when she saw it or deny it. It was also said: to show the power of Allah, glorified is He, and the greatness of His dominion, in a miracle He would bring about in her throne.

An 'ifrit of the jinn said: The 'ifrit is the strong rebellious one. It has two forms: 'ifrit and 'ifriyah; whoever says 'ifrit makes its plural 'afarit, and whoever says 'ifriyah makes its plural 'afarit... [sic: 'afarit/'afarit as in the source]. Wahb said: his name was Kawdhi. Shu'ayb al-Jaba'i said: the name of the 'ifrit was Dhakwan. Ibn Abbas said: the 'ifrit is the calamity. Al-Dahhak said: he is the wicked one. Rabi': the coarse one. Al-Farra': the strong and mighty. Al-Kisa'i: the strange one, and he recited:

"A devil among them said, an 'ifrit: what is the matter with you, no staying nor overnight stay?"

Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi read: "qala 'ifriyah."

Abu Ahmad ibn Fanjawayh informed me: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Samurah al-Baghawi told us: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Shadhan al-Baghdadi told us: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Sahl told us:

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 27, verses 27–44 (part 2 of 2):

Abd al-Rahman al-Bahtari narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Uthman narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Qurashi, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), that he used to recite: "Qala 'Ifritun min al-jinn" (A demon of the jinn said). Al-'Ifritah is the one who is strong and bold among the strong and bold, whose parents had not borne any child before him, and who had not borne any child himself.

"I will bring it to you before you rise from your place," that is, from your assembly in which you judge. Ibn Abbas said: He had every morning an assembly in which he judged until the end of the day.

"And indeed I am strong enough for it," to carry it, "and trustworthy" regarding what is in it of jewels. Then Sulayman (peace be upon him) said: "I want something quicker than this."

"He who had knowledge of the Scripture said..." The scholars differed about him. Some of them said: he was Jibril (peace be upon him), an angel whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, strengthened His Prophet Sulayman (peace be upon him) with.

Others said: rather, he was a man from the children of Adam.

Then they differed about him. Most of the mufassirun (exegetes) said: he was Asif ibn Barkhiya ibn Shamma' ibn Makiya, and he was a siddiq (truthful one) who knew the Greatest Name (al-ism al-a'zam), which, when called upon by it, answers, and when asked by it, gives.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Makhlad ibn Ja'far al-Baqirhi informed us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Alawiyyah narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Isa narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Juwaybir and Muqatil narrated to us, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Asif said to Sulayman (peace be upon him), when he had prayed and supplicated to Allah, the Exalted: "Widen your eyes until your gaze reaches its limit." So Sulayman (peace be upon him) widened his eye and looked toward Yemen, and Asif supplicated, and Allah sent the angels, who carried the throne from beneath the earth, cutting through the earth with great force, until the earth was split open before Sulayman (peace be upon him) and the throne appeared before him.

The scholars differed about the supplication with which Asif called upon Allah when bringing the throne.

Aisha narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the Greatest Name of Allah, with which Asif supplicated, is: 'Ya Hayy, ya Qayyum' (O Ever-Living, O Self-Subsisting)." [114] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/204.]]

Uthman ibn Matar narrated from al-Zuhri, who said: the supplication of "He who had knowledge of the Scripture" was: "O our God and God of everything, one God, there is no god but You, bring me her throne." He said: So it was presented to him before him. Mujahid said: "O Possessor of Majesty and Honour." Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Talha ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, both saying: Abu Bakr ibn Mujahid narrated to us, saying: Isma'il narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Isma'il, from Ibn Zayd, who said: "He who had knowledge of the Scripture" was a righteous man who was on one of the islands of the sea. He went out that day to look: Who inhabits the earth? Does Allah, Mighty and Majestic, get worshipped or not? He found Sulayman (peace be upon him), so he supplicated with one of the names of Allah, and behold, the throne was being carried, and it was brought to Sulayman before his gaze returned to him.

And from him, from Mujahid, who said: al-Bizzi and Ibn Harb narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Bazzah claimed that the name of "He who had knowledge of the Scripture" was Ustuwm. Some of them said: he was a man from Himyar called Dabbah.

Qatadah said: his name was Bulayha. Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir said: Rather, it was Sulayman himself. Indeed, people think that he had a name [of Allah] with him, and that is not so. Rather, he was a learned man from the Children of Israel, whom Allah had given knowledge and understanding. He said: "I will bring it to you before your gaze returns to you." Sulayman (peace be upon him) said: "Bring it." He said: "You are the Prophet, son of a Prophet, and no one is more honoured before Allah than you, nor more able to grant what is asked. If you supplicate to Allah and ask Him, it will be done for you." He said: "You have spoken the truth." So he did that, and the throne was brought at once.

As for His saying, "before your gaze returns to you," the scholars differed about its meaning. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: It means before it comes back to you from the farthest place you have left, namely that it reaches you from as far as your gaze can reach. Qatadah said: before the person comes to you from the distance of sight.

Wahb said: You widen your eyes, and your gaze does not reach its limit until I place it before you.

Mujahid said: It means continuing to look until the gaze returns weary.

From him also: It means the extent of your sight between you and al-Hirah, and at that time it was in Kindah.

From Qatadah: It means that he sends a messenger to the limit of his sight, and the messenger does not return until it is brought.

"So when he saw it" (meaning Sulayman, peace be upon him, saw the throne) "placed beside him," brought to him from Ma'rib to Syria in the time it takes the gaze to return, he said: "This is of the bounty of my Lord, to test me: whether I am grateful for His blessing or ungrateful." That is, I will not be grateful for it. "And whoever is grateful, is only grateful for his own self," he benefits no one but himself, since by his gratitude he merits the completion and continuance of the blessing, for gratitude is a tether for existing blessings and a snare for lost blessings.

"And whoever is ungrateful, then indeed my Lord is Free of need, Generous," bestowing favour upon the one who is ungrateful for His blessings.

He said: "Disguise her throne for her," change it, add to it and subtract from it, and make its top its bottom and its bottom its top, "let us see whether she will be guided to her throne," so that she recognises it, "or whether she will be among those who are not guided," those who do not recognise it.

Sulayman (peace be upon him) was prompted to do this, as Wahb, Muhammad ibn Ka'b and others from the People of the Book mentioned: The devils feared that Sulayman would marry her, and then she would reveal to him the secrets of the jinn, and they would no longer be free of subjection to Sulayman and his descendants after him. So they wanted to make him averse to her, and they spoke ill of her, saying: "There is something wrong in her intellect, and her leg is like a donkey's hoof." So Sulayman (peace be upon him) wished to test her intellect by altering her throne, and to see her legs by the building of the palace (al-sarh).

"So when she came, it was said: 'Is your throne like this?' She said: 'It is as if it were it.'" He compared it to it, and she had left it behind her in a house behind seven locked doors, with the keys with her. So she neither confirmed nor denied it, and Sulayman (peace be upon him) knew her complete intellect.

Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: They confused her, and she confused them, answering them according to their question. Had they said to her, "This is your throne," she would have said, "Yes."

Then Sulayman (peace be upon him) said: "And we were given the knowledge (of Allah and His power over whatever He wills) before this woman, and we were Muslims." This is the saying of Mujahid. Others said: it means "we were given the knowledge of her Islam and her coming in obedience, before her coming, and we were Muslims," obedient and submissive.

Some said: this is from the speech of Bilqis when she saw her throne with Sulayman (peace be upon him). She said: "It seems to be it," and "we were given the knowledge" of the truth of Sulayman's prophethood through the signs mentioned before this verse, namely what she tested of the matter of the gift and the messengers, "and we were Muslims," that is, submissive to you and obedient to your command, before we came to you.

"And it prevented her from what she used to worship besides Allah," namely the sun, by her not worshipping Allah. On this view, the word "ma" (what) is in the nominative position (marfu').

Some said: the meaning is: Sulayman prevented her from what she used to worship besides Allah, that is, it prevented her and stood between her and it. And if it were said: "Allah prevented her from that by guiding her to Islam," that would be a correct interpretation. On these two interpretations, the word "ma" is in the accusative position (manṣub).

"Indeed she was from a disbelieving people." It was said to her: "Enter the palace" (al-sarh), the verse. This is because when Bilqis came to him, Sulayman ordered the devils, and they built for him a palace (sarh), that is a castle of glass, as if it were water in its whiteness. It was also said that the sarh is the courtyard of a house. He made water flow beneath it and placed in it every creature of the sea, fish and others. Then he set his throne in its centre, and he sat upon it, and birds, jinn and humans hovered around him. He only ordered the building of this palace because the devils said to one another: "Allah has subjected to Sulayman what He has subjected, and Bilqis, queen of Sheba, will marry him and bear him a son, and then we will never be free of servitude forever." So they wanted to make him averse to her, and they said: "Her husband is a donkey-legged man, and she has hairy shins, because her mother was from the jinn." So he wished to know the truth of that and to look at her feet and shins.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from some of the people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: He only built the palace to test her intellect and understanding, to see her through it, just as she had done when she sent to him the male and female servants, so that he might distinguish males from females, and she might see him through that.

When Bilqis came, it was said to her: "Enter the palace." When she saw it, she thought it was a deep water (lujjah), which is the greatest part of the water. Ibn Jurayj said: meaning a sea.

"She uncovered her shins," in order to wade through it to Sulayman (peace be upon him). Sulayman looked and found that she had the most beautiful shins and feet of all people, except that she had hairy shins. When Sulayman saw that, he turned his gaze away from her and called out to her: "It is a palace, smooth and glassy" (qawarir), and not a sea. When she sat down, she said: "O Sulayman, I want to ask you about something."

He said: "Ask."

She said: "Tell me about what is water that is neither from the earth nor from the sky." Whenever Sulayman was asked about something he did not know, he asked mankind about it; if they had knowledge of it, well and good, otherwise he asked the jinn, and if they knew, well and good, otherwise he asked the devils. So he asked the devils about this, and they said to him: "This is easier than that. Let horses run and then fill the vessels with their sweat."

Sulayman said to her: "It is the sweat of horses." She said: "You have spoken the truth." Then she said: "Tell me about the colour of the Lord." Sulayman (peace be upon him) jumped from his throne, fell prostrate and fainted. She departed from him, and his armies scattered. A messenger came to him and said: "O Sulayman, your Lord says to you: what is your matter?"

He said: "O Lord, You know best what she said." He said: "Allah commands you to return to your throne and send for her, and for those present with her from your armies and hers, and ask her and them about what you were asked." Sulayman (peace be upon him) did so. When they entered upon him, he said to her: "About what did you ask me?" She said: "I asked you about water that is neither from the earth nor from the sky, and you answered."

He said: "And about what else did you ask me?"

She said: "I asked you about nothing but this." He said: "Ask the troops." They said the same as she had said. Allah, the Exalted, made them forget that, and that sufficed Sulayman (peace be upon him) as an answer.

Then Sulayman invited her to Islam, and she had seen the condition of the throne and the palace, so she responded and said: "My Lord, I have wronged myself" (by disbelief) "and I have submitted with Sulayman to Allah, Lord of the worlds." Her Islam was good.

The scholars differed about her matter after her Islam. Most of them said: When she became Muslim, Sulayman wanted to marry her. When he intended that, he disliked what he saw of the abundance of hair on her shins and said: "How ugly this is!" He asked mankind: "What removes this?" They said: "The razor." The woman said: "No iron has ever touched me." So Sulayman disliked the razor and said: "It will cut her shins." He asked the jinn, and they said: "We do not know." Then he asked the devils, and they hesitated, then said: "We will devise for you a way so that she becomes like white silver." So they made for her depilatory cream (nurah) and the bathhouse (hammam).

Ibn Abbas said: That was the first day that depilatory cream was seen, and Sulayman (peace be upon him) married her.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Nasrawayh narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Imran ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Maymun al-Makki narrated to us, saying: Abu Harun al-Attar narrated to me, from Abu Hafs al-Abbar, from Isma'il ibn Abi Burdah, from Abu Musa, who traced it back to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The first to make bathhouses was Sulayman ibn Dawud (peace be upon him). When he leaned his back against the walls and their heat touched him, he said: 'Ah, from the punishment of Allah!'" [115] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/210.]]

They said: When Sulayman married her, he loved her very much, and he confirmed her in her kingdom. He commanded the jinn, and they built for her in the land of Yemen three castles, the like of which people had never seen in height and beauty. They were: Salhun, Sun and Amdan. Then Sulayman (peace be upon him) would visit her once a month, after he had returned her to her kingdom, and he would stay with her for three days, travelling early from Syria to Yemen and from Yemen to Syria. She bore him children, as is reported.

Ibn Abi Ishaq narrated from some people of knowledge, from Wahb, who said: They claim that Sulayman ibn Dawud (peace be upon him) said to Bilqis when she had become Muslim and he had finished with her affair: "Choose a man from your people, and I will marry you to him."

She said: "And someone like me, O Prophet of Allah, marries men, when I had the kingdom and authority among my people that I had?"

He said: "Yes, indeed in Islam there is nothing but that, and it is not right for you to forbid what Allah has made lawful for you."

She said: "Marry me, if it must be, to Dhu Tubba', the king of Hamadan." So he married her to him, then sent her back to Yemen and gave her husband Dhu Tubba' authority over Yemen. He summoned Zawba'ah, the commander of the jinn of Yemen, and said: "Do for Dhu Tubba' whatever I have appointed you to do."

He said: So he made for Dhu Tubba' crafts in Yemen, and he continued to work for him there, doing whatever he wished, until Sulayman ibn Dawud (peace be upon him) died. When a year had passed and the jinn realised that Sulayman (peace be upon him) had died, a man of them came, travelled through Tihamah, and when he was in the heart of Yemen, he cried out at the top of his voice: "O company of jinn, indeed King Sulayman has died, so lift your hands (from your labour)!" He said: So the devils went to two great stones and inscribed on them a writing in the Musnad script: "We built Salhin, enduring [seventy-seven autumns], and we built Sarwah and Marwah [and Banyun, Hadiyah, Hind and Hunaydah, and seven lofty houses in Baqa'ah, and Talthum in Buraydah; and had it not been for the crier in Tihamah, we would have left in al-Bawn a government]," and "Salhin, Sarwah, Marwah, Baynun, Hind, Hunaydah and Talthum are castles in Yemen which the devils built for Dhu Tubba'." [[The manuscript text is garbled; the correction is from Tafsir al-Tabari.]] Then they lifted their hands, departed and scattered, and the kingdom of Dhu Tubba' and the kingdom of Bilqis came to an end along with the kingdom of Sulayman (peace be upon him). [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 1/351.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 27, verse 27–44 (part 1 of 2):

Solomon said to the hoopoe, "We shall see whether you have told the truth, or whether you are among the liars." So the hoopoe guided them to the water, and they dug wells and the people and the animals drank, for they had been thirsty. Then Solomon wrote a letter: "From Allah's servant Solomon son of David (peace be upon him) to Bilqis, queen of Sheba: Peace be upon whoever follows the guidance. To proceed: do not exalt yourselves against me, and come to me in submission (muslimin)."

Ibn Jurayj said: Solomon added nothing to what Allah related in His Book: "Indeed it is... and indeed it is..."

Mansur said: It used to be said: Solomon was the most eloquent of people in his letter and the most concise in dictation. Then he recited: "Indeed it is from Solomon, and indeed it is: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful."

Qatada said: Likewise the prophets (peace be upon them) would write in short sentences, neither lengthening nor multiplying words. When he finished the letter, he sealed it with musk and stamped it with his signet ring, and said to the hoopoe: "Take this letter of mine and throw it to them, then withdraw from them and stay near them, and see what they return", i.e., what answer they send back.

Ibn Zayd said: In the verse there is inversion of order; its meaning is: "Take this letter of mine and throw it to them, and see what they return, then withdraw from them", i.e., turn away, like His saying "then he turned away to the shade" (i.e., went back to it). So the hoopoe took the letter and brought it to Bilqis. She was in a land called Ma'rib, three days from Sana'a. He reached her in her palace, and its doors had been locked, for whenever she slept she would lock the doors and take the keys and place them under her head, and retire to her bed. The hoopoe came to her while she was sleeping on her back, and dropped the letter onto her chest. This is the saying of Qatada.

Muqatil said: The hoopoe carried the letter in its beak and flew until it alighted above the woman's head, while her commanders and soldiers surrounded her. It fluttered for a while while the people watched, until the woman raised her head, and it dropped the letter into her lap.

Ibn Munabbih and Ibn Zayd said: She had a window facing the sun, through which the sun would shine when it rose; whenever she looked at it she would prostrate to it. The hoopoe came to that window and blocked it with his wing, so the sun rose without her knowing. When she delayed in noticing the sun, she stood up to look, and he threw the sheet to her.

They said: Bilqis took the letter. She was a literate, Arabic-writing woman from the people of Tubba' ibn Sharahil al-Himyari. When she saw the seal she trembled and submitted, because Solomon's kingdom was in his ring, and she knew that the one who sent this letter was greater in kingship than she, since a king whose messengers are birds is truly a great king. She read the letter, and the hoopoe withdrew not far off. Then she came and sat on her royal throne and gathered the chiefs of her people, who were twelve thousand commanders, each commander having a hundred thousand fighters.

Qatada, Muqatil and al-Thumali said: Her council of advisers was three hundred and thirteen men, each one over ten thousand.

They said: They came and took their seats, and Bilqis said to them: "O chiefs, indeed there has been thrown to me a noble letter."

Qatada said: "Noble" is good; its counterpart is His saying "and a noble station" (Q. 26:58). Ibn Abbas said: "Noble" means honourable by the honour of its sender. Al-Dahhak said: She called it noble because it was sealed, as is shown by what:

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us: Ahmad ibn Shadhan informed us: Jubaʻawayh ibn Muhammad told us: Salih ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Marwan told us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn Abbas, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "The dignity of a letter is its seal."

And Abdullah ibn Hamid informed me: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: 'Amr told us: Abu 'Isa Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Tirmidhi told me: Ishaq ibn Mansur told us: Mu'adh ibn Hisham told us: my father told me, from Qatada, from Anas, who said: When the Prophet of Allah ﷺ wished to write to the non-Arabs, it was said to him: "The non-Arabs will not accept a letter unless it bears a seal." So he had a ring made, and it is as if I see the whiteness of it on his hand.

Ibn al-Muqaffa' said: Whoever writes to his brother a letter and does not seal it has treated it lightly, for the seal is a seal. It was also said: she called it noble because it began with "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful... Indeed it is from Solomon, and indeed it is: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Do not exalt yourselves against me, and come to me in submission." Ashhab al-'Uqayli read: "illa taghluw 'alayya" with a dotted ghayn, and "wa'tuni muslimin" means believers, obedient.

She said: "O chiefs." Ibn Abbas said: With Bilqis were a hundred thousand qayls, each qayl with a hundred thousand, and a qayl is below the supreme king. "Advise me in my matter": give me your counsel concerning what has befallen me, and answer me on what I consult you about. "I would not decide a matter" means I would not judge or conclude it, "until you witness" me, i.e., attend me.

They replied to her: "We are people of strength in battle and possessors of mighty might in war, but the command is yours, O queen, so consider what you will command"; that is, you will find us obedient to your order.

Then Bilqis said to them, when they offered themselves for war: "Indeed, when kings enter a town by force and conquest, they corrupt it, and make the honoured of its people abased", i.e., they humiliate its nobles and great ones so that the affair may be settled for them. The report of her words ended here, and Allah, glorified is He, confirmed her saying, and said: "And thus do they act."

Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to me, saying: my father (may Allah have mercy on him) recited:

Indeed kings are a affliction wherever they alight,
so let there be no shade for you in their vicinity.
What do you hope from people who, when angered,
oppress you, and if you please them, they tire of you?
If you praise them, they deem you a dupe they deceive,
and they find you burdensome as one finds a burden heavy.
So be self-sufficient in Allah, from their doors forever,
for standing at their doors is humiliation.

[[What follows: Tabaqat al-Mufassirin, al-Suyuti, p. 37.]]

"And I am sending them a gift." That is because Bilqis was shrewd, having been tested and having tested others, so she said to the chiefs of her people: "I am sending to Solomon and his people a gift, to win him over with it regarding my kingdom, and to test him with it: is he a king?" If he is a king, he will accept the gift and withdraw; but if he is a prophet, he will not accept the gift, and will not be pleased with anything from us except that we follow his religion. So she sent him a servant boy and servant girls.

Ibn Abbas said: She dressed them in one garment, so that the male could not be distinguished from the female.

Mujahid said: She dressed the boys in the dress of girls and the girls in the dress of boys. They differed on their number: Muqatil said: a hundred male servants and a hundred female servants. Mujahid said: two hundred boys and two hundred girls. Al-Kalbi said: ten boys and ten girls. Wahb and others said: five hundred boys and five hundred girls.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Ibn Hanash told us: Ibn Fanjawayh told us: Salamah told us: 'Abd al-Razzaq told us: Ma'mar informed us, from Thabit al-Bunani, regarding His saying "And I am sending them a gift": She sent him sheets of gold in cases of brocade. When this reached Solomon, he commanded the jinn, who coated the bricks with gold, and then he ordered them cast into the road. When they came, they saw them strewn along the road everywhere. They said: "We have come bearing something, yet here are things lying about which no one even looks at." So what they had brought seemed small in their eyes. It was also said: there were four gold bricks. Wahb and others among the People of the Book said: Bilqis chose five hundred girls and five hundred boys; she dressed the girls in the clothing of boys, the tunics and belts, and dressed the boys in the clothing of girls, and put bracelets of gold on their forearms, and collars of gold around their necks, and earrings and ornaments set with various jewels; she loaded the girls on five hundred mares and the boys on five hundred mules, each horse with a golden bridle set with jewels and covers of coloured brocade. She also sent him five hundred bricks of gold and five hundred bricks of silver, and a crown studded with pearls and rising rubies, and she also sent musk, ambergris, and aloes-wood. She took a casket and placed in it a single unpierced pearl and a bent-holed jewel with a twisted hole, and summoned a man of the nobles of her people called al-Mundhir ibn 'Amr, and attached to him men of her people who were men of opinion and intellect, and she wrote a letter with him, a copy of the gift, and said: "If you are a prophet, distinguish between the male servants and the female servants, tell what is in the casket before you open it, and pierce the pearl with an even hole and thread a string through it." She commanded the boys, saying: "When Solomon speaks to you, speak to him in a manner with feminine softness and effeminacy, resembling women's speech," and she commanded the girls to speak to him in a harsh manner resembling men's speech. Then she said to the messenger: "Look at the man when you enter upon him: if he looks at you with a look of anger, know that he is a king, and let his appearance not overawe you, for I am more honoured than he; but if you see the man cheerful and gentle, know that he is a prophet sent, so understand his words and return the answer."

The messenger set off with the gifts, and the hoopoe came hastening to Solomon (peace be upon him) and informed him of the whole matter. Solomon (peace be upon him) commanded the jinn to strike bricks of gold and silver, and they did so. Then he commanded them to spread out from the place where he was to a distance of nine farsakhs a single courtyard paved with bricks of gold and silver, and to make around the courtyard a wall with battlements of gold and silver, and they did. Then he said: "Which of the animals is finer than what you have seen on land and sea?" They said: "O prophet of Allah, we have seen animals in the sea of such-and-such, striped, separate, of varied colours, having wings, manes and forelocks." He said: "Bring them to me at once," and they were brought. He said: "Tie them on the right side of the courtyard and on its left, upon the bricks of gold and silver, and throw their fodder to them."

Then he said to the jinn: "Bring me your children," and a great multitude gathered; he set them up on the right side of the courtyard and its left. Then Solomon (peace be upon him) sat in his assembly upon his throne, and forty thousand chairs were placed for him on his right and the same number on his left. He commanded the devils to line up in ranks for farsakhs, and commanded mankind to line up for farsakhs, and commanded the wild beasts, the predators, the vermin and the birds to line up for farsakhs on his right and his left.

When the people saw the courtyard and looked at the kingdom of Solomon (peace be upon him), and saw animals whose like their eyes had never seen dunging upon bricks of gold and silver, their souls seemed small to them, and they remained with what they had of gifts.

In some reports, when Solomon (peace be upon him) commanded that the courtyard be paved with bricks of gold and silver, he commanded them to leave on their road a place the size of the bricks they had with them; so when the envoys saw the place of the bricks empty while the whole ground was paved, they feared they would be accused of this, so they threw what they had into that place.

They said: Then they came, and when they saw the devils they looked at a wondrous place and were frightened. The devils said to them: "Pass on, there is no harm upon you." So they kept passing by rank after rank of jinn, mankind, birds, predators and wild beasts, until they stood before Solomon (peace be upon him). Solomon looked at them with a pleasant look and an open face, and said: "What is behind you?" The leader of the people informed him of what they had come for, and gave him the queen's letter. He looked into it and said: "Where is the casket?" It was brought to him, and he shook it. Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him and told him what was in the casket, and he said: "Indeed there is in it a single unpierced pearl and a jewel with a bent hole, twisted in its perforation." The messenger said: "You have spoken truly; so pierce the pearl and thread the string through the jewel." Solomon (peace be upon him) said: "Who will pierce it for me?" He asked mankind, but they had no knowledge of that; then he asked the jinn, and they had no knowledge of that; then he asked the devils, and they said: "Send for the termite." The termite came, took a hair in its mouth and entered the hole, and came out the other side. Solomon (peace be upon him) said to it: "What is your need?" It said: "Make my sustenance in the wood." He said: "That is yours." Then he said: "Who will thread this jewel?" A white worm said: "I will, O messenger of Allah." The worm took the thread in its mouth and entered the hole until it came out the other side. Solomon said: "What is your need?" It said: "Make my sustenance in fruits." He said: "That is yours."

Then he distinguished between the girls and the boys by commanding them to wash their faces and hands. The girl would take the water from the vessel with one hand, then pour it onto the other hand, then strike the face with it; the boy would take it from the vessel and strike his face with it. The girl would pour water over the inner part of her forearm, the boy over the back of the forearm; the girl would pour the water in a pouring stream, and the boy would let the water run down his hand in a trickle. Thus he distinguished between them by that. Then Solomon (peace be upon him) returned the gift.

He said: "Are you supplying me with wealth?" The readers differed concerning it: Hamza and Ya'qub read "atumiddunni" with a single doubled nun, while the others read it with two light nuns and omitted the yā'; Ibn 'Amir, 'Asim, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read with the yā', and the rest with it retained.

"What Allah has given me is better than what He has given you; rather, you rejoice in your gift." That is because you are people of boasting in worldly things and of arrogance through them, and you know nothing else; and this world is not among my needs, for Allah, glorified is He, has empowered me over it and given me in it what He has given no one else, and despite that He has honoured me with religion, prophethood and wisdom. Then he said to al-Mundhir ibn 'Amr, the leader of the delegation: "Return to them with the gift, for we shall certainly come to them with armies they cannot withstand, and we shall certainly expel them from it", i.e., from their land and kingdom, "abased, and they will be humbled" (sāghirūn), i.e., humiliated, if they do not come to me in submission.

Wahb and others among the People of the Book said: When Bilqis's envoys returned to her from Solomon (peace be upon him), she said: "By Allah, I have known that this is no mere king, and we have no power against him, and we can do nothing by rivalling him." She sent to Solomon: "I am coming to you with the kings of my people, so that I may see what your command is and what you call to of your religion." Then she ordered her throne to be placed within seven chambers, one inside another, at the end of the palace, among seven palaces of hers; then she closed the doors behind it and set guards to watch over it. Then she said to the one she left in charge of her realm: "Guard what is before you and my royal throne, so that no one reaches it or adorns it until I come to you." Then she commanded a herald, who proclaimed among the people of her kingdom, informing them of the departure, and she set out toward Solomon with twelve thousand qayls of the kings of Yemen, under each qayl many thousands.

Ibn Abbas said: Solomon was a man of awe who did not begin anything until he was asked about it. One day he went out and sat on his royal throne, and saw a cloud of dust near him, and said: "What is this?"

They said: "Bilqis, O prophet of Allah."

He said: "Has she come down to us to this place?" Ibn Abbas said: The distance between Kufa and al-Hira was about one farsakh. Then Solomon turned to his soldiers and said: "Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?" That is, believers. Ibn Abbas said: obedient.

The scholars differed about the reason for which Solomon (peace be upon him) commanded the bringing of the throne. Most of them said: because Solomon (peace be upon him) knew that if she became Muslim, what was hers would become unlawful to him, so he wished to take her throne before it became unlawful for him to take it by her Islam.

Qatada said: Because its description had pleased him when the hoopoe described it, so he loved to see it.

Ibn Zayd said: He wished to test her intellect, by commanding that it be altered, to see whether she would recognise it when she saw it or deny it. It was also said: to show the power of Allah, glorified is He, and the greatness of His dominion, in a miracle He would bring about in her throne.

An 'ifrit of the jinn said: The 'ifrit is the strong rebellious one. It has two forms: 'ifrit and 'ifriyah; whoever says 'ifrit makes its plural 'afarit, and whoever says 'ifriyah makes its plural 'afarit... [sic: 'afarit/'afarit as in the source]. Wahb said: his name was Kawdhi. Shu'ayb al-Jaba'i said: the name of the 'ifrit was Dhakwan. Ibn Abbas said: the 'ifrit is the calamity. Al-Dahhak said: he is the wicked one. Rabi': the coarse one. Al-Farra': the strong and mighty. Al-Kisa'i: the strange one, and he recited:

"A devil among them said, an 'ifrit: what is the matter with you, no staying nor overnight stay?"

Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi read: "qala 'ifriyah."

Abu Ahmad ibn Fanjawayh informed me: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Samurah al-Baghawi told us: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Shadhan al-Baghdadi told us: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Sahl told us:

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 27, verses 27–44 (part 2 of 2):

Abd al-Rahman al-Bahtari narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Uthman narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Qurashi, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), that he used to recite: "Qala 'Ifritun min al-jinn" (A demon of the jinn said). Al-'Ifritah is the one who is strong and bold among the strong and bold, whose parents had not borne any child before him, and who had not borne any child himself.

"I will bring it to you before you rise from your place," that is, from your assembly in which you judge. Ibn Abbas said: He had every morning an assembly in which he judged until the end of the day.

"And indeed I am strong enough for it," to carry it, "and trustworthy" regarding what is in it of jewels. Then Sulayman (peace be upon him) said: "I want something quicker than this."

"He who had knowledge of the Scripture said..." The scholars differed about him. Some of them said: he was Jibril (peace be upon him), an angel whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, strengthened His Prophet Sulayman (peace be upon him) with.

Others said: rather, he was a man from the children of Adam.

Then they differed about him. Most of the mufassirun (exegetes) said: he was Asif ibn Barkhiya ibn Shamma' ibn Makiya, and he was a siddiq (truthful one) who knew the Greatest Name (al-ism al-a'zam), which, when called upon by it, answers, and when asked by it, gives.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Makhlad ibn Ja'far al-Baqirhi informed us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Alawiyyah narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Isa narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Juwaybir and Muqatil narrated to us, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Asif said to Sulayman (peace be upon him), when he had prayed and supplicated to Allah, the Exalted: "Widen your eyes until your gaze reaches its limit." So Sulayman (peace be upon him) widened his eye and looked toward Yemen, and Asif supplicated, and Allah sent the angels, who carried the throne from beneath the earth, cutting through the earth with great force, until the earth was split open before Sulayman (peace be upon him) and the throne appeared before him.

The scholars differed about the supplication with which Asif called upon Allah when bringing the throne.

Aisha narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the Greatest Name of Allah, with which Asif supplicated, is: 'Ya Hayy, ya Qayyum' (O Ever-Living, O Self-Subsisting)." [114] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/204.]]

Uthman ibn Matar narrated from al-Zuhri, who said: the supplication of "He who had knowledge of the Scripture" was: "O our God and God of everything, one God, there is no god but You, bring me her throne." He said: So it was presented to him before him. Mujahid said: "O Possessor of Majesty and Honour." Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Talha ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, both saying: Abu Bakr ibn Mujahid narrated to us, saying: Isma'il narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Isma'il, from Ibn Zayd, who said: "He who had knowledge of the Scripture" was a righteous man who was on one of the islands of the sea. He went out that day to look: Who inhabits the earth? Does Allah, Mighty and Majestic, get worshipped or not? He found Sulayman (peace be upon him), so he supplicated with one of the names of Allah, and behold, the throne was being carried, and it was brought to Sulayman before his gaze returned to him.

And from him, from Mujahid, who said: al-Bizzi and Ibn Harb narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Bazzah claimed that the name of "He who had knowledge of the Scripture" was Ustuwm. Some of them said: he was a man from Himyar called Dabbah.

Qatadah said: his name was Bulayha. Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir said: Rather, it was Sulayman himself. Indeed, people think that he had a name [of Allah] with him, and that is not so. Rather, he was a learned man from the Children of Israel, whom Allah had given knowledge and understanding. He said: "I will bring it to you before your gaze returns to you." Sulayman (peace be upon him) said: "Bring it." He said: "You are the Prophet, son of a Prophet, and no one is more honoured before Allah than you, nor more able to grant what is asked. If you supplicate to Allah and ask Him, it will be done for you." He said: "You have spoken the truth." So he did that, and the throne was brought at once.

As for His saying, "before your gaze returns to you," the scholars differed about its meaning. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: It means before it comes back to you from the farthest place you have left, namely that it reaches you from as far as your gaze can reach. Qatadah said: before the person comes to you from the distance of sight.

Wahb said: You widen your eyes, and your gaze does not reach its limit until I place it before you.

Mujahid said: It means continuing to look until the gaze returns weary.

From him also: It means the extent of your sight between you and al-Hirah, and at that time it was in Kindah.

From Qatadah: It means that he sends a messenger to the limit of his sight, and the messenger does not return until it is brought.

"So when he saw it" (meaning Sulayman, peace be upon him, saw the throne) "placed beside him," brought to him from Ma'rib to Syria in the time it takes the gaze to return, he said: "This is of the bounty of my Lord, to test me: whether I am grateful for His blessing or ungrateful." That is, I will not be grateful for it. "And whoever is grateful, is only grateful for his own self," he benefits no one but himself, since by his gratitude he merits the completion and continuance of the blessing, for gratitude is a tether for existing blessings and a snare for lost blessings.

"And whoever is ungrateful, then indeed my Lord is Free of need, Generous," bestowing favour upon the one who is ungrateful for His blessings.

He said: "Disguise her throne for her," change it, add to it and subtract from it, and make its top its bottom and its bottom its top, "let us see whether she will be guided to her throne," so that she recognises it, "or whether she will be among those who are not guided," those who do not recognise it.

Sulayman (peace be upon him) was prompted to do this, as Wahb, Muhammad ibn Ka'b and others from the People of the Book mentioned: The devils feared that Sulayman would marry her, and then she would reveal to him the secrets of the jinn, and they would no longer be free of subjection to Sulayman and his descendants after him. So they wanted to make him averse to her, and they spoke ill of her, saying: "There is something wrong in her intellect, and her leg is like a donkey's hoof." So Sulayman (peace be upon him) wished to test her intellect by altering her throne, and to see her legs by the building of the palace (al-sarh).

"So when she came, it was said: 'Is your throne like this?' She said: 'It is as if it were it.'" He compared it to it, and she had left it behind her in a house behind seven locked doors, with the keys with her. So she neither confirmed nor denied it, and Sulayman (peace be upon him) knew her complete intellect.

Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: They confused her, and she confused them, answering them according to their question. Had they said to her, "This is your throne," she would have said, "Yes."

Then Sulayman (peace be upon him) said: "And we were given the knowledge (of Allah and His power over whatever He wills) before this woman, and we were Muslims." This is the saying of Mujahid. Others said: it means "we were given the knowledge of her Islam and her coming in obedience, before her coming, and we were Muslims," obedient and submissive.

Some said: this is from the speech of Bilqis when she saw her throne with Sulayman (peace be upon him). She said: "It seems to be it," and "we were given the knowledge" of the truth of Sulayman's prophethood through the signs mentioned before this verse, namely what she tested of the matter of the gift and the messengers, "and we were Muslims," that is, submissive to you and obedient to your command, before we came to you.

"And it prevented her from what she used to worship besides Allah," namely the sun, by her not worshipping Allah. On this view, the word "ma" (what) is in the nominative position (marfu').

Some said: the meaning is: Sulayman prevented her from what she used to worship besides Allah, that is, it prevented her and stood between her and it. And if it were said: "Allah prevented her from that by guiding her to Islam," that would be a correct interpretation. On these two interpretations, the word "ma" is in the accusative position (manṣub).

"Indeed she was from a disbelieving people." It was said to her: "Enter the palace" (al-sarh), the verse. This is because when Bilqis came to him, Sulayman ordered the devils, and they built for him a palace (sarh), that is a castle of glass, as if it were water in its whiteness. It was also said that the sarh is the courtyard of a house. He made water flow beneath it and placed in it every creature of the sea, fish and others. Then he set his throne in its centre, and he sat upon it, and birds, jinn and humans hovered around him. He only ordered the building of this palace because the devils said to one another: "Allah has subjected to Sulayman what He has subjected, and Bilqis, queen of Sheba, will marry him and bear him a son, and then we will never be free of servitude forever." So they wanted to make him averse to her, and they said: "Her husband is a donkey-legged man, and she has hairy shins, because her mother was from the jinn." So he wished to know the truth of that and to look at her feet and shins.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from some of the people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: He only built the palace to test her intellect and understanding, to see her through it, just as she had done when she sent to him the male and female servants, so that he might distinguish males from females, and she might see him through that.

When Bilqis came, it was said to her: "Enter the palace." When she saw it, she thought it was a deep water (lujjah), which is the greatest part of the water. Ibn Jurayj said: meaning a sea.

"She uncovered her shins," in order to wade through it to Sulayman (peace be upon him). Sulayman looked and found that she had the most beautiful shins and feet of all people, except that she had hairy shins. When Sulayman saw that, he turned his gaze away from her and called out to her: "It is a palace, smooth and glassy" (qawarir), and not a sea. When she sat down, she said: "O Sulayman, I want to ask you about something."

He said: "Ask."

She said: "Tell me about what is water that is neither from the earth nor from the sky." Whenever Sulayman was asked about something he did not know, he asked mankind about it; if they had knowledge of it, well and good, otherwise he asked the jinn, and if they knew, well and good, otherwise he asked the devils. So he asked the devils about this, and they said to him: "This is easier than that. Let horses run and then fill the vessels with their sweat."

Sulayman said to her: "It is the sweat of horses." She said: "You have spoken the truth." Then she said: "Tell me about the colour of the Lord." Sulayman (peace be upon him) jumped from his throne, fell prostrate and fainted. She departed from him, and his armies scattered. A messenger came to him and said: "O Sulayman, your Lord says to you: what is your matter?"

He said: "O Lord, You know best what she said." He said: "Allah commands you to return to your throne and send for her, and for those present with her from your armies and hers, and ask her and them about what you were asked." Sulayman (peace be upon him) did so. When they entered upon him, he said to her: "About what did you ask me?" She said: "I asked you about water that is neither from the earth nor from the sky, and you answered."

He said: "And about what else did you ask me?"

She said: "I asked you about nothing but this." He said: "Ask the troops." They said the same as she had said. Allah, the Exalted, made them forget that, and that sufficed Sulayman (peace be upon him) as an answer.

Then Sulayman invited her to Islam, and she had seen the condition of the throne and the palace, so she responded and said: "My Lord, I have wronged myself" (by disbelief) "and I have submitted with Sulayman to Allah, Lord of the worlds." Her Islam was good.

The scholars differed about her matter after her Islam. Most of them said: When she became Muslim, Sulayman wanted to marry her. When he intended that, he disliked what he saw of the abundance of hair on her shins and said: "How ugly this is!" He asked mankind: "What removes this?" They said: "The razor." The woman said: "No iron has ever touched me." So Sulayman disliked the razor and said: "It will cut her shins." He asked the jinn, and they said: "We do not know." Then he asked the devils, and they hesitated, then said: "We will devise for you a way so that she becomes like white silver." So they made for her depilatory cream (nurah) and the bathhouse (hammam).

Ibn Abbas said: That was the first day that depilatory cream was seen, and Sulayman (peace be upon him) married her.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Nasrawayh narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Imran ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Maymun al-Makki narrated to us, saying: Abu Harun al-Attar narrated to me, from Abu Hafs al-Abbar, from Isma'il ibn Abi Burdah, from Abu Musa, who traced it back to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The first to make bathhouses was Sulayman ibn Dawud (peace be upon him). When he leaned his back against the walls and their heat touched him, he said: 'Ah, from the punishment of Allah!'" [115] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/210.]]

They said: When Sulayman married her, he loved her very much, and he confirmed her in her kingdom. He commanded the jinn, and they built for her in the land of Yemen three castles, the like of which people had never seen in height and beauty. They were: Salhun, Sun and Amdan. Then Sulayman (peace be upon him) would visit her once a month, after he had returned her to her kingdom, and he would stay with her for three days, travelling early from Syria to Yemen and from Yemen to Syria. She bore him children, as is reported.

Ibn Abi Ishaq narrated from some people of knowledge, from Wahb, who said: They claim that Sulayman ibn Dawud (peace be upon him) said to Bilqis when she had become Muslim and he had finished with her affair: "Choose a man from your people, and I will marry you to him."

She said: "And someone like me, O Prophet of Allah, marries men, when I had the kingdom and authority among my people that I had?"

He said: "Yes, indeed in Islam there is nothing but that, and it is not right for you to forbid what Allah has made lawful for you."

She said: "Marry me, if it must be, to Dhu Tubba', the king of Hamadan." So he married her to him, then sent her back to Yemen and gave her husband Dhu Tubba' authority over Yemen. He summoned Zawba'ah, the commander of the jinn of Yemen, and said: "Do for Dhu Tubba' whatever I have appointed you to do."

He said: So he made for Dhu Tubba' crafts in Yemen, and he continued to work for him there, doing whatever he wished, until Sulayman ibn Dawud (peace be upon him) died. When a year had passed and the jinn realised that Sulayman (peace be upon him) had died, a man of them came, travelled through Tihamah, and when he was in the heart of Yemen, he cried out at the top of his voice: "O company of jinn, indeed King Sulayman has died, so lift your hands (from your labour)!" He said: So the devils went to two great stones and inscribed on them a writing in the Musnad script: "We built Salhin, enduring [seventy-seven autumns], and we built Sarwah and Marwah [and Banyun, Hadiyah, Hind and Hunaydah, and seven lofty houses in Baqa'ah, and Talthum in Buraydah; and had it not been for the crier in Tihamah, we would have left in al-Bawn a government]," and "Salhin, Sarwah, Marwah, Baynun, Hind, Hunaydah and Talthum are castles in Yemen which the devils built for Dhu Tubba'." [[The manuscript text is garbled; the correction is from Tafsir al-Tabari.]] Then they lifted their hands, departed and scattered, and the kingdom of Dhu Tubba' and the kingdom of Bilqis came to an end along with the kingdom of Sulayman (peace be upon him). [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 1/351.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 27, verse 27–44 (part 1 of 2):

Solomon said to the hoopoe, "We shall see whether you have told the truth, or whether you are among the liars." So the hoopoe guided them to the water, and they dug wells and the people and the animals drank, for they had been thirsty. Then Solomon wrote a letter: "From Allah's servant Solomon son of David (peace be upon him) to Bilqis, queen of Sheba: Peace be upon whoever follows the guidance. To proceed: do not exalt yourselves against me, and come to me in submission (muslimin)."

Ibn Jurayj said: Solomon added nothing to what Allah related in His Book: "Indeed it is... and indeed it is..."

Mansur said: It used to be said: Solomon was the most eloquent of people in his letter and the most concise in dictation. Then he recited: "Indeed it is from Solomon, and indeed it is: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful."

Qatada said: Likewise the prophets (peace be upon them) would write in short sentences, neither lengthening nor multiplying words. When he finished the letter, he sealed it with musk and stamped it with his signet ring, and said to the hoopoe: "Take this letter of mine and throw it to them, then withdraw from them and stay near them, and see what they return", i.e., what answer they send back.

Ibn Zayd said: In the verse there is inversion of order; its meaning is: "Take this letter of mine and throw it to them, and see what they return, then withdraw from them", i.e., turn away, like His saying "then he turned away to the shade" (i.e., went back to it). So the hoopoe took the letter and brought it to Bilqis. She was in a land called Ma'rib, three days from Sana'a. He reached her in her palace, and its doors had been locked, for whenever she slept she would lock the doors and take the keys and place them under her head, and retire to her bed. The hoopoe came to her while she was sleeping on her back, and dropped the letter onto her chest. This is the saying of Qatada.

Muqatil said: The hoopoe carried the letter in its beak and flew until it alighted above the woman's head, while her commanders and soldiers surrounded her. It fluttered for a while while the people watched, until the woman raised her head, and it dropped the letter into her lap.

Ibn Munabbih and Ibn Zayd said: She had a window facing the sun, through which the sun would shine when it rose; whenever she looked at it she would prostrate to it. The hoopoe came to that window and blocked it with his wing, so the sun rose without her knowing. When she delayed in noticing the sun, she stood up to look, and he threw the sheet to her.

They said: Bilqis took the letter. She was a literate, Arabic-writing woman from the people of Tubba' ibn Sharahil al-Himyari. When she saw the seal she trembled and submitted, because Solomon's kingdom was in his ring, and she knew that the one who sent this letter was greater in kingship than she, since a king whose messengers are birds is truly a great king. She read the letter, and the hoopoe withdrew not far off. Then she came and sat on her royal throne and gathered the chiefs of her people, who were twelve thousand commanders, each commander having a hundred thousand fighters.

Qatada, Muqatil and al-Thumali said: Her council of advisers was three hundred and thirteen men, each one over ten thousand.

They said: They came and took their seats, and Bilqis said to them: "O chiefs, indeed there has been thrown to me a noble letter."

Qatada said: "Noble" is good; its counterpart is His saying "and a noble station" (Q. 26:58). Ibn Abbas said: "Noble" means honourable by the honour of its sender. Al-Dahhak said: She called it noble because it was sealed, as is shown by what:

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us: Ahmad ibn Shadhan informed us: Jubaʻawayh ibn Muhammad told us: Salih ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Marwan told us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn Abbas, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "The dignity of a letter is its seal."

And Abdullah ibn Hamid informed me: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: 'Amr told us: Abu 'Isa Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Tirmidhi told me: Ishaq ibn Mansur told us: Mu'adh ibn Hisham told us: my father told me, from Qatada, from Anas, who said: When the Prophet of Allah ﷺ wished to write to the non-Arabs, it was said to him: "The non-Arabs will not accept a letter unless it bears a seal." So he had a ring made, and it is as if I see the whiteness of it on his hand.

Ibn al-Muqaffa' said: Whoever writes to his brother a letter and does not seal it has treated it lightly, for the seal is a seal. It was also said: she called it noble because it began with "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful... Indeed it is from Solomon, and indeed it is: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Do not exalt yourselves against me, and come to me in submission." Ashhab al-'Uqayli read: "illa taghluw 'alayya" with a dotted ghayn, and "wa'tuni muslimin" means believers, obedient.

She said: "O chiefs." Ibn Abbas said: With Bilqis were a hundred thousand qayls, each qayl with a hundred thousand, and a qayl is below the supreme king. "Advise me in my matter": give me your counsel concerning what has befallen me, and answer me on what I consult you about. "I would not decide a matter" means I would not judge or conclude it, "until you witness" me, i.e., attend me.

They replied to her: "We are people of strength in battle and possessors of mighty might in war, but the command is yours, O queen, so consider what you will command"; that is, you will find us obedient to your order.

Then Bilqis said to them, when they offered themselves for war: "Indeed, when kings enter a town by force and conquest, they corrupt it, and make the honoured of its people abased", i.e., they humiliate its nobles and great ones so that the affair may be settled for them. The report of her words ended here, and Allah, glorified is He, confirmed her saying, and said: "And thus do they act."

Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to me, saying: my father (may Allah have mercy on him) recited:

Indeed kings are a affliction wherever they alight,
so let there be no shade for you in their vicinity.
What do you hope from people who, when angered,
oppress you, and if you please them, they tire of you?
If you praise them, they deem you a dupe they deceive,
and they find you burdensome as one finds a burden heavy.
So be self-sufficient in Allah, from their doors forever,
for standing at their doors is humiliation.

[[What follows: Tabaqat al-Mufassirin, al-Suyuti, p. 37.]]

"And I am sending them a gift." That is because Bilqis was shrewd, having been tested and having tested others, so she said to the chiefs of her people: "I am sending to Solomon and his people a gift, to win him over with it regarding my kingdom, and to test him with it: is he a king?" If he is a king, he will accept the gift and withdraw; but if he is a prophet, he will not accept the gift, and will not be pleased with anything from us except that we follow his religion. So she sent him a servant boy and servant girls.

Ibn Abbas said: She dressed them in one garment, so that the male could not be distinguished from the female.

Mujahid said: She dressed the boys in the dress of girls and the girls in the dress of boys. They differed on their number: Muqatil said: a hundred male servants and a hundred female servants. Mujahid said: two hundred boys and two hundred girls. Al-Kalbi said: ten boys and ten girls. Wahb and others said: five hundred boys and five hundred girls.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Ibn Hanash told us: Ibn Fanjawayh told us: Salamah told us: 'Abd al-Razzaq told us: Ma'mar informed us, from Thabit al-Bunani, regarding His saying "And I am sending them a gift": She sent him sheets of gold in cases of brocade. When this reached Solomon, he commanded the jinn, who coated the bricks with gold, and then he ordered them cast into the road. When they came, they saw them strewn along the road everywhere. They said: "We have come bearing something, yet here are things lying about which no one even looks at." So what they had brought seemed small in their eyes. It was also said: there were four gold bricks. Wahb and others among the People of the Book said: Bilqis chose five hundred girls and five hundred boys; she dressed the girls in the clothing of boys, the tunics and belts, and dressed the boys in the clothing of girls, and put bracelets of gold on their forearms, and collars of gold around their necks, and earrings and ornaments set with various jewels; she loaded the girls on five hundred mares and the boys on five hundred mules, each horse with a golden bridle set with jewels and covers of coloured brocade. She also sent him five hundred bricks of gold and five hundred bricks of silver, and a crown studded with pearls and rising rubies, and she also sent musk, ambergris, and aloes-wood. She took a casket and placed in it a single unpierced pearl and a bent-holed jewel with a twisted hole, and summoned a man of the nobles of her people called al-Mundhir ibn 'Amr, and attached to him men of her people who were men of opinion and intellect, and she wrote a letter with him, a copy of the gift, and said: "If you are a prophet, distinguish between the male servants and the female servants, tell what is in the casket before you open it, and pierce the pearl with an even hole and thread a string through it." She commanded the boys, saying: "When Solomon speaks to you, speak to him in a manner with feminine softness and effeminacy, resembling women's speech," and she commanded the girls to speak to him in a harsh manner resembling men's speech. Then she said to the messenger: "Look at the man when you enter upon him: if he looks at you with a look of anger, know that he is a king, and let his appearance not overawe you, for I am more honoured than he; but if you see the man cheerful and gentle, know that he is a prophet sent, so understand his words and return the answer."

The messenger set off with the gifts, and the hoopoe came hastening to Solomon (peace be upon him) and informed him of the whole matter. Solomon (peace be upon him) commanded the jinn to strike bricks of gold and silver, and they did so. Then he commanded them to spread out from the place where he was to a distance of nine farsakhs a single courtyard paved with bricks of gold and silver, and to make around the courtyard a wall with battlements of gold and silver, and they did. Then he said: "Which of the animals is finer than what you have seen on land and sea?" They said: "O prophet of Allah, we have seen animals in the sea of such-and-such, striped, separate, of varied colours, having wings, manes and forelocks." He said: "Bring them to me at once," and they were brought. He said: "Tie them on the right side of the courtyard and on its left, upon the bricks of gold and silver, and throw their fodder to them."

Then he said to the jinn: "Bring me your children," and a great multitude gathered; he set them up on the right side of the courtyard and its left. Then Solomon (peace be upon him) sat in his assembly upon his throne, and forty thousand chairs were placed for him on his right and the same number on his left. He commanded the devils to line up in ranks for farsakhs, and commanded mankind to line up for farsakhs, and commanded the wild beasts, the predators, the vermin and the birds to line up for farsakhs on his right and his left.

When the people saw the courtyard and looked at the kingdom of Solomon (peace be upon him), and saw animals whose like their eyes had never seen dunging upon bricks of gold and silver, their souls seemed small to them, and they remained with what they had of gifts.

In some reports, when Solomon (peace be upon him) commanded that the courtyard be paved with bricks of gold and silver, he commanded them to leave on their road a place the size of the bricks they had with them; so when the envoys saw the place of the bricks empty while the whole ground was paved, they feared they would be accused of this, so they threw what they had into that place.

They said: Then they came, and when they saw the devils they looked at a wondrous place and were frightened. The devils said to them: "Pass on, there is no harm upon you." So they kept passing by rank after rank of jinn, mankind, birds, predators and wild beasts, until they stood before Solomon (peace be upon him). Solomon looked at them with a pleasant look and an open face, and said: "What is behind you?" The leader of the people informed him of what they had come for, and gave him the queen's letter. He looked into it and said: "Where is the casket?" It was brought to him, and he shook it. Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him and told him what was in the casket, and he said: "Indeed there is in it a single unpierced pearl and a jewel with a bent hole, twisted in its perforation." The messenger said: "You have spoken truly; so pierce the pearl and thread the string through the jewel." Solomon (peace be upon him) said: "Who will pierce it for me?" He asked mankind, but they had no knowledge of that; then he asked the jinn, and they had no knowledge of that; then he asked the devils, and they said: "Send for the termite." The termite came, took a hair in its mouth and entered the hole, and came out the other side. Solomon (peace be upon him) said to it: "What is your need?" It said: "Make my sustenance in the wood." He said: "That is yours." Then he said: "Who will thread this jewel?" A white worm said: "I will, O messenger of Allah." The worm took the thread in its mouth and entered the hole until it came out the other side. Solomon said: "What is your need?" It said: "Make my sustenance in fruits." He said: "That is yours."

Then he distinguished between the girls and the boys by commanding them to wash their faces and hands. The girl would take the water from the vessel with one hand, then pour it onto the other hand, then strike the face with it; the boy would take it from the vessel and strike his face with it. The girl would pour water over the inner part of her forearm, the boy over the back of the forearm; the girl would pour the water in a pouring stream, and the boy would let the water run down his hand in a trickle. Thus he distinguished between them by that. Then Solomon (peace be upon him) returned the gift.

He said: "Are you supplying me with wealth?" The readers differed concerning it: Hamza and Ya'qub read "atumiddunni" with a single doubled nun, while the others read it with two light nuns and omitted the yā'; Ibn 'Amir, 'Asim, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read with the yā', and the rest with it retained.

"What Allah has given me is better than what He has given you; rather, you rejoice in your gift." That is because you are people of boasting in worldly things and of arrogance through them, and you know nothing else; and this world is not among my needs, for Allah, glorified is He, has empowered me over it and given me in it what He has given no one else, and despite that He has honoured me with religion, prophethood and wisdom. Then he said to al-Mundhir ibn 'Amr, the leader of the delegation: "Return to them with the gift, for we shall certainly come to them with armies they cannot withstand, and we shall certainly expel them from it", i.e., from their land and kingdom, "abased, and they will be humbled" (sāghirūn), i.e., humiliated, if they do not come to me in submission.

Wahb and others among the People of the Book said: When Bilqis's envoys returned to her from Solomon (peace be upon him), she said: "By Allah, I have known that this is no mere king, and we have no power against him, and we can do nothing by rivalling him."
