﴿So their faces will be thrown into the Fire.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: they will be cast down. Al-Dahhak said: they will be flung. Abu al-'Aliya said: they will be overturned. It has been said that they will be told: ﴿Are you recompensed except for what you used to do?﴾

God, glory be to Him, says to His Prophet, Muhammad (peace be upon him): Say: ﴿I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city, which He has made sacred,﴾ meaning Makkah, which He made a sanctuary and a place of safety. Shedding blood unlawfully is not permitted in it, no one is wronged in it, it is not to be hunted, its game is not to be hunted, and its plants are not to be cut. Ibn 'Abbas recited "allati harramaha" (which He has made sacred), referring to the city.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 27, verse 83–93 (part 2 of 2):

﴿And His is every thing, by creation and by ownership.﴾ ﴿I have been commanded to be among the Muslims, and to recite the Qur'an. So whoever is guided, he is only guided for his own soul; and whoever goes astray, say: I am only one of the warners.﴾ ﴿And upon us is only the conveyance (of the message).﴾ [[Surat Ya-Sin: 17.]] It was abrogated by the verse of fighting (naskh, abrogation: the replacement of a earlier ruling by a later one).

﴿And say: Praise belongs to Allah﴾ for His blessings. ﴿He will show you His signs﴾, meaning on the Day of Badr. Its parallel is in Surat al-Anbiya': ﴿I will show you My signs, so do not seek to hasten them.﴾

Mujahid said: ﴿He will show you His signs﴾ within yourselves, in the heavens and the earth, and in provision. His proof is His saying: ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves﴾ [[Surat Fussilat: 53.]] and His saying: ﴿And on the earth are signs for those who are certain, and within yourselves﴾ [[Surat adh-Dhariyat: 20–21.]] ﴿So you will recognize them.﴾ ﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what you do.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 27, verses 83–93 (part 1 of 2):

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And on the Day when We shall gather from every nation a troop of those who denied Our signs, and they will be driven in ranks.﴾ A group of those who deny. Their first is held back until their last, so that they gather together, and then they are driven to the Fire. Ibn 'Abbas said: "yuza'un" means they are pushed. ﴿Until, when they have come, He will say: "Did you deny My signs without comprehending them in knowledge, or what was it that you were doing?"﴾ God, glory be to Him, says to them: Did you deny My signs without having encompassed them in knowledge, and without having known their true knowing? "Or what was it that you were doing" regarding them, by denial or by affirmation? It has also been said that this is a rebuke: what were you doing when you did not search into them and did not reflect upon them? ﴿And the word will fall upon them because of their wrongdoing,﴾ meaning the punishment becomes due because they associated partners, ﴿so they will not speak.﴾ Because their mouths will be sealed. Most of the exegetes said: "so they will not speak" with a proof or an excuse. Its parallel is the saying of God, glory be to Him: ﴿This is a day on which they will not speak, nor will they be permitted to make excuses.﴾ [Surah al-Mursalat: 35–36.] ﴿Have they not seen that We made the night for them to rest therein, and the day giving sight? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ Those who affirm and so take heed. The words of the Exalted: ﴿And on the Day when the Trumpet is blown﴾ — this is the first blast.

Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Yazid al-Sayrafi informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn Harb told us, saying: Asbat told us, saying: Salman al-Tamimi [in the second copy: al-Taymi] told us, from Aslam al-'Ijli, from Bishr ibn Shaghaf, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: A Bedouin came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and asked him about the Sur, and he said: "A horn into which it is blown." [Musnad Ahmad: 2/162.] [121].

Mujahid said: the Sur is like the shape of a trumpet. It has also been said that it is in the language of the people of Yemen, and most of the exegetes hold this view. What supports it is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "How can I be at ease, when the holder of the horn has put the horn to his mouth and bowed his forehead, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow?" [Kanz al-'Ummal: 14/625, no. 39743.] [122].

Qatada and Abu 'Ubaida said: it is the plural of "surah" (form), one says "surah" and "sur," and "sur" is like the "sur" of a building or a mosque, and its plural is "sur" and "su'ur." Abu 'Ubaida recited:
"I travelled towards her on the high parts of the walls."
So the meaning of the verse is: and the forms of creation are blown.

A comprehensive and sound report has come concerning the manner of the blowing of the Sur, which is what:

Imam Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Mihrajani informed us by reading to him, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim al-Shafi'i in Baghdad, saying: Abu Qilaba al-Raqqashi informed me, saying: Abu 'Asim al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad informed me, from Isma'il ibn Rafi', from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from a man of the Ansar, from Abu Hurayra, who said:

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When God, Mighty and Majestic, finished creating the heavens and the earth, He created the Sur and gave it to Israfil, who placed it at his mouth, his gaze fixed on the Plain, waiting for when he will be told."

I said: O Messenger of God, what is the Sur? He said: "The horn." I said: What is it like? He said: "Great. By Him who sent me with the truth, its width is like the breadth of the heavens and the earth. It is blown with three blasts: the first is the blast of terror, the second is the blast of swooning, and the third is the blast of rising for the Lord of the worlds. God, Mighty and Majestic, commands Israfil (peace be upon him) concerning the first blast, and he says: 'Blow the blast of terror,' and so those in the heavens and the earth are terrified, except whom God wills. He commands him, and he prolongs it and extends it. This is what God, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿They await only one shout, with no pause.﴾ God sets the mountains in motion, so they pass like clouds and become a mirage. The earth is shaken with its inhabitants with a violent shaking, so it is like a ship moored in the sea, struck by the waves and tossed by the winds, or like a lamp hanging from the Throne, swayed by the winds. This is what God, Mighty and Majestic, refers to in His words: ﴿On the Day when the Quaker quakes, followed by the Follower; hearts on that day will be trembling.﴾ Then the earth stretches out with the people upon its back. Nursing women forget their infants, pregnant women give birth, children turn grey, and the devils flee in terror until they reach the horizons, where the angels meet them and strike their faces. They turn back, and the people flee in retreat, calling out to one another. This is what God, Mighty and Majestic, refers to in His words: ﴿The Day of Calling out, the Day when you turn your backs and flee; you will have no protector from God.﴾"

"While they are in this state, the earth splits open from one side to another, or they see a great matter the like of which they have never seen, and the anguish and terror that God alone knows seize them. Then they look at the sky, and it is like molten brass. Then it is split open, its stars scattered and its sun and moon eclipsed."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The dead on that day will know something of that." [123].

Abu Hurayra said: O Messenger of God, who is it that God excepted when He said: ﴿And whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified, except whom God wills﴾?

He (ﷺ) said: "Those are the martyrs. Terror reaches only the living, and they are alive with their Lord, being provided for. God protected them from the terror of that Day and made them secure. It is a punishment God sends upon the worst of His creation. This is what God refers to when He says: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord; indeed, the quaking of the Hour is a tremendous thing,﴾ up to His words: ﴿But the punishment of God is severe.﴾"

They remain in that affliction as long as God wills, except that it lasts long for them. Then God commands Israfil, and he blows the blast of swooning, and ﴿whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth swoons, except whom God wills.﴾ When they are gathered, the Angel of Death comes to the Almighty and says: "The people of the heavens and the earth have died, except whom You will." God, glory be to Him, who knows best, says: "Who remains?" He says: "O Lord, You remain, the Living who does not die. The bearers of the Throne remain, Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil remain, and I remain." God says: "Jibril and Mika'il will die." So they die. Then the Throne speaks and says: "O Lord, will Jibril and Mika'il die?" He says: "Be silent. I have decreed death upon everyone beneath My Throne, and so they will die."

Then the Angel of Death comes and says: "O Lord, Jibril and Mika'il have died." He says, and He knows best who remains: "Who remains?" He says: "You remain, the Living who does not die, and the bearers of Your Throne remain, and I remain." He says: "Let the bearers of My Throne die," and they die. Then God commands the Throne, and it takes the Sur from Israfil, and he dies.

Then the Angel of Death comes and says: "O Lord, the bearers of Your Throne have died." He says, and He knows best who remains: "Who remains?" He says: "You remain, the Living who does not die, and I remain." He says: "You are a creature among My creatures, whom I created for a purpose. Die," and he dies. When no one remains but God, the One, the Unique, the Eternal Refuge, ﴿who begets not, nor is He begotten, and none is comparable to Him﴾, and He was the last as He was the first, He folds up the heavens ﴿like the folding of a scroll for writings.﴾

Then He says: "I am the Almighty. ﴿To whom belongs the dominion this Day?﴾" and no one answers Him. Then He, blessed and exalted, glorified in His names, says: ﴿To God, the One, the Subduer.﴾ ﴿The Day the earth will be changed into another earth﴾ ﴿and the heavens folded up.﴾ He spreads them out in a spreading, then stretches them like a tanned hide, ﴿in which you will see no crookedness or unevenness.﴾

Then God drives the creatures with one driving, and they are in this changed earth in the same state they were in at first: whoever was in its belly is in its belly, and whoever was on its back is on its back. Then God sends down upon them water from beneath the Throne like the semen of men, and then He commands the clouds to send down rain for forty days, until it reaches twelve cubits above them. God, glory be to Him, commands the bodies to grow like the growth of the truffles and the growth of herbs, until their bodies are complete as they were. God, glory be to Him, says: "Let the bearers of the Throne live," and they live. Then God, may He be exalted, says: "Let Jibril and Mika'il live," and they live. Then God commands Israfil, and he takes the Sur and places it at his mouth. Then God calls the souls and they are brought; the souls of the believers shine with light, and the others are dark. He seizes them all and then casts them into the Sur. Then God, glory be to Him, commands Israfil to blow a blast for the Resurrection, and the souls come out like bees that have filled what is in the heavens and the earth. God, glory be to Him, says: "Every soul shall return to its body," and the souls enter the nostrils, and then they move through the bodies as poison moves through one who has been stung.

Then the earth splits open over them swiftly. I am the first whom the earth splits open for. You will come out of it to your Lord, hastening, naked, barefoot, uncircumcised, ﴿hurrying toward the summoner.﴾ The disbelievers will say: "This is a difficult day." [124].

The words of the Exalted: ﴿So they are terrified﴾ — meaning "so they will be terrified." The Arabs do this in places where "idha" (when) fits, because "idha" is followed by a verb in the past or the present, as in your saying: "I will visit you when you visit me" and "I will visit you when you are visiting me." ﴿Whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, except whom God wills﴾ — that they not be terrified. We have already mentioned in the preceding report that they are the martyrs. ﴿And all come to Him, humbled.﴾ Al-A'mash, Hamza, Khalaf and Hafs recited "atawhu" with a short vowel, as a finite verb meaning "they came to Him," coordinated with His words "fa-fazi'a" (so they were terrified), and "atawhu" following the reading of Ibn Mas'ud.

Muhammad ibn Nu'aym informed us, saying: al-Husayn [in the second copy: al-Hasan] ibn Ayyub told us, saying: 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz told us, saying: Abu 'Ubayd told us, saying: Hisham told us, from Mughira, from Ibrahim. And Muhammad ibn 'Abdus informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Jahm told us, saying: al-Farra' told us, saying: 'Iddah (a number of people) told me, among them al-Mufaddal al-Dabbi, Qays and Abu Bakr, all from Jahsh ibn Ziyad al-Dabbi, both from Tamim ibn Hudhlam, who said: I recited to 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud "wa-kullun atawhu dakhirin" with a lengthened alif, and he said: "wa-kullun atawhu" with a short vowel.

The rest of the reciters recited with the lengthening of the alif and a damma on the ta', in the pattern of "fa'iluhu," as in His words: ﴿And every one of them will come to Him alone on the Day of Resurrection.﴾ [Surah Maryam: 95.] This is the reading of 'Ali, may God be pleased with him.

"Dakhirin" means humbled.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And you will see the mountains﴾ — O Muhammad — ﴿you think them fixed,﴾ standing, stationary, settled in their place. ﴿Yet they pass by as the clouds pass.﴾ When they strike the earth, they level it with them.

Al-Qutaybi said: That is because the mountains are gathered and move, and in the sight of the eye they appear to be standing while they are moving. Likewise, everything great and every large gathering that the eye cannot take in, because of its multitude and immensity, and whose extremities are counted, appears to the observer to be standing still while it is moving. The poet referred to this in describing an army:
"O troop, like a mountain you think them standing still for a halt, while the riding camels pace."

"Ṣun'a Allah" (the work of God) is in the accusative as a verbal noun. It has also been said that it is in the accusative as an incitement, meaning: know and see ﴿the work of God, who perfected everything.﴾ That is, He made everything firm. Qatada said: He made everything good. ﴿Indeed, He is Aware of what you do.﴾ The people of Kufa recited "taf'aluna" with the ta', and others with the ya'. Abu 'Ubayda chose the ya' with the statement "atawhu," since it is a report about them.

﴿Whoever comes with good﴾ — meaning whoever arrives before God with faith. Abu Ma'shar said: Ibrahim used to swear without any exception that the good deed is: "There is no god but God." Qatada said: with sincerity.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Shanbah told us, saying: 'Ubayd [in the second copy: 'Abd] Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Mansur told us, saying: Sahl ibn Bishr told us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Sulayman told us, saying: Sa'd ibn Sa'id told us, saying: I heard 'Ali ibn al-Husayn say: A man went out to fight in the way of God, and whenever he was alone in a place he would say: "There is no god but God, alone, without partner." Then one day, while he was in the land of the Romans, in a place of reeds and dry grass, he raised his voice saying: "There is no god but God, alone, without partner." A man came out to him on a horse, wearing white garments, and said: "O servant of God, what is this you have said?" He said: "I said what you heard. By Him in whose hand my soul is, it is the word of which God, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Whoever comes with good﴾."

﴿Then he will have better than it, and they will be secure from the terror of that Day.﴾

Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-'Abbasi informed me, saying: al-Qadi Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn 'Uthman [al-Nasibi in Baghdad] informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Subay'i told us in Aleppo, saying: al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim al-Jassas told me, saying: al-Husayn ibn al-Hakam informed us, saying: Isma'il ibn Aban told us, from [Fudayl] ibn al-Zubayr, from Abu Dawud al-Subay'i, from Abu 'Abd Allah al-Hudhali, who said: I entered upon 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and he said: "O servant of God, shall I tell you of the good deed, whoever comes with which God will admit into Paradise, and of the evil deed, whoever comes with which God will hurl him into the Fire, and no deed will be accepted with it?"

I said: Yes. He said: "The good deed is our love, and the evil deed is our hatred."

﴿Then he will have better than it﴾ — that is, from this good deed he will have better on the Day of Resurrection, which is the reward and security from punishment.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿Then he will have better than it﴾ means that from it good reaches him. Al-Hasan said: its meaning is that he has good from it. 'Ikrima and Ibn Jurayj said: As for whether he has better than faith, no. There is nothing better than "There is no god but God," but he has good from it. Ibn 'Abbas also said: ﴿Then he will have better than it﴾ means the reward, because obedience is the servant's action and the reward is God's action, glory be to Him.

It has been said: God, Mighty and Majestic, accepts his faith and his good deeds, and God's acceptance is better than the servant's deed. It has also been said: ﴿Then he will have better than it﴾ means the good pleasure of God, glory be to Him. God, may He be exalted, says: ﴿And the good pleasure of God is greater.﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 72.]

Muhammad ibn Ka'b and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: ﴿Then he will have better than it﴾ means the multiplication. God gives the good deed as ten times over, and so this is better than it. Ibn Ka'b and Ibn Zayd were right in their interpretations, because multiplication has distinctive features: the servant is questioned about his deed but is not questioned about the multiplication; Satan has a path to his deed but has no path to the multiplication; the adversaries have no hope in the multiplication; the abode of the good deed is this world, and the abode of multiplication is Paradise; and Paradise is by the servant's merit, while multiplication is as befits the generosity of the Lord.

﴿And they will be secure from the terror of that Day.﴾ The people of Kufa recited "fazi'in" with tanwin and "yawma'idhin" with a fatha on the mim, which is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud. The rest of the reciters read it with the genitive construction. Abu 'Ubayd chose it, saying: because it is the more general of the two interpretations, that security is from all the terror of that Day. But if one says "min fazi'a yawma'idhin," it becomes as though it were a terror of a particular kind. Al-Farra' also chose this, saying: because it is a known terror. Do you not see that He said: ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾? So He made it definite. If you give it the genitive construction, it becomes definite, and this is more pleasing to me.

﴿And whoever comes with evil﴾ — meaning association with partners.

Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, saying: Makki ibn 'Abdan informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Hashim told us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman told us, from Sufyan, from Abu al-Mahjal, from Abu Ma'shar, from Ibrahim, concerning ﴿whoever comes with good﴾, he said: "There is no god but God." And ﴿whoever comes with evil﴾, he said: "Association with partners."

'Abd ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb al-Bayhaqi informed us, saying: Bishr ibn Musa told us, saying: Rawh told us, from Habib ibn al-Shahid, from al-Hasan, who said: The price of Paradise is "There is no god but God."

﴿So their faces will be thrown into the Fire.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: they will be cast down. Al-Dahhak said: they will be flung. Abu al-'Aliya said: they will be overturned. It has been said that they will be told: ﴿Are you recompensed except for what you used to do?﴾

Ibn 'Abbas recited "allati harramaha" (which He has made sacred), referring to the city.

They turn back, and the people flee in retreat, calling out to one another. This is what God, Mighty and Majestic, refers to in His words: ﴿The Day of Calling out, the Day when you turn your backs and flee; you will have no protector from God.﴾"

"While they are in this state, the earth splits open from one side to another, or they see a great matter the like of which they have never seen, and the anguish and terror that God alone knows seize them. Then they look at the sky, and it is like molten brass. Then it is split open, its stars scattered and its sun and moon eclipsed."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The dead on that day will know something of that." [123].

Abu Hurayra said: O Messenger of God, who is it that God excepted when He said: ﴿And whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified, except whom God wills﴾?

He (ﷺ) said: "Those are the martyrs. Terror reaches only the living, and they are alive with their Lord, being provided for. God protected them from the terror of that Day and made them secure. It is a punishment God sends upon the worst of His creation. This is what God refers to when He says: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord; indeed, the quaking of the Hour is a tremendous thing,﴾ up to His words: ﴿But the punishment of God is severe.﴾"

They remain in that affliction as long as God wills, except that it lasts long for them. Then God commands Israfil, and he blows the blast of swooning, and ﴿whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth swoons, except whom God wills.﴾ When they are gathered, the Angel of Death comes to the Almighty and says: "The people of the heavens and the earth have died, except whom You will." God, glory be to Him, who knows best, says: "Who remains?" He says: "O Lord, You remain, the Living who does not die. The bearers of the Throne remain, Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil remain, and I remain." God says: "Jibril and Mika'il will die." So they die. Then the Throne speaks and says: "O Lord, will Jibril and Mika'il die?" He says: "Be silent. I have decreed death upon everyone beneath My Throne, and so they will die."

Then the Angel of Death comes and says: "O Lord, Jibril and Mika'il have died." He says, and He knows best who remains: "Who remains?" He says: "You remain, the Living who does not die, and the bearers of Your Throne remain, and I remain." He says: "Let the bearers of My Throne die," and they die. Then God commands the Throne, and it takes the Sur from Israfil, and he dies.

Then the Angel of Death comes and says: "O Lord, the bearers of Your Throne have died." He says, and He knows best who remains: "Who remains?" He says: "You remain, the Living who does not die, and I remain." He says: "You are a creature among My creatures, whom I created for a purpose. Die," and he dies. When no one remains but God, the One, the Unique, the Eternal Refuge, ﴿who begets not, nor is He begotten, and none is comparable to Him﴾, and He was the last as He was the first, He folds up the heavens ﴿like the folding of a scroll for writings.﴾

Then He says: "I am the Almighty. ﴿To whom belongs the dominion this Day?﴾" and no one answers Him. Then He, blessed and exalted, glorified in His names, says: ﴿To God, the One, the Subduer.﴾ ﴿The Day the earth will be changed into another earth﴾ ﴿and the heavens folded up.﴾ He spreads them out in a spreading, then stretches them like a tanned hide, ﴿in which you will see no crookedness or unevenness.﴾

Then God drives the creatures with one driving, and they are in this changed earth in the same state they were in at first: whoever was in its belly is in its belly, and whoever was on its back is on its back. Then God sends down upon them water from beneath the Throne like the semen of men, and then He commands the clouds to send down rain for forty days, until it reaches twelve cubits above them. God, glory be to Him, commands the bodies to grow like the growth of the truffles and the growth of herbs, until their bodies are complete as they were. God, glory be to Him, says: "Let the bearers of the Throne live," and they live. Then God, may He be exalted, says: "Let Jibril and Mika'il live," and they live. Then God commands Israfil, and he takes the Sur and places it at his mouth. Then God calls the souls and they are brought; the souls of the believers shine with light, and the others are dark. He seizes them all and then casts them into the Sur. Then God, glory be to Him, commands Israfil to blow a blast for the Resurrection, and the souls come out like bees that have filled what is in the heavens and the earth. God, glory be to Him, says: "Every soul shall return to its body," and the souls enter the nostrils, and then they move through the bodies as poison moves through one who has been stung.

Then the earth splits open over them swiftly. I am the first whom the earth splits open for. You will come out of it to your Lord, hastening, naked, barefoot, uncircumcised, ﴿hurrying toward the summoner.﴾ The disbelievers will say: "This is a difficult day." [124].

The words of the Exalted: ﴿So they are terrified﴾ — meaning "so they will be terrified." The Arabs do this in places where "idha" (when) fits, because "idha" is followed by a verb in the past or the present, as in your saying: "I will visit you when you visit me" and "I will visit you when you are visiting me." ﴿Whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, except whom God wills﴾ — that they not be terrified. We have already mentioned in the preceding report that they are the martyrs. ﴿And all come to Him, humbled.﴾ Al-A'mash, Hamza, Khalaf and Hafs recited "atawhu" with a short vowel, as a finite verb meaning "they came to Him," coordinated with His words "fa-fazi'a" (so they were terrified), and "atawhu" following the reading of Ibn Mas'ud.

Muhammad ibn Nu'aym informed us, saying: al-Husayn [in the second copy: al-Hasan] ibn Ayyub told us, saying: 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz told us, saying: Abu 'Ubayd told us, saying: Hisham told us, from Mughira, from Ibrahim. And Muhammad ibn 'Abdus informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Jahm told us, saying: al-Farra' told us, saying: 'Iddah (a number of people) told me, among them al-Mufaddal al-Dabbi, Qays and Abu Bakr, all from Jahsh ibn Ziyad al-Dabbi, both from Tamim ibn Hudhlam, who said: I recited to 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud "wa-kullun atawhu dakhirin" with a lengthened alif, and he said: "wa-kullun atawhu" with a short vowel.

The rest of the reciters recited with the lengthening of the alif and a damma on the ta', in the pattern of "fa'iluhu," as in His words: ﴿And every one of them will come to Him alone on the Day of Resurrection.﴾ [Surah Maryam: 95.] This is the reading of 'Ali, may God be pleased with him.

"Dakhirin" means humbled.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And you will see the mountains﴾ — O Muhammad — ﴿you think them fixed,﴾ standing, stationary, settled in their place. ﴿Yet they pass by as the clouds pass.﴾ When they strike the earth, they level it with them.

Al-Qutaybi said: That is because the mountains are gathered and move, and in the sight of the eye they appear to be standing while they are moving. Likewise, everything great and every large gathering that the eye cannot take in, because of its multitude and immensity, and whose extremities are counted, appears to the observer to be standing still while it is moving. The poet referred to this in describing an army:
"O troop, like a mountain you think them standing still for a halt, while the riding camels pace."

"Ṣun'a Allah" (the work of God) is in the accusative as a verbal noun. It has also been said that it is in the accusative as an incitement, meaning: know and see ﴿the work of God, who perfected everything.﴾ That is, He made everything firm. Qatada said: He made everything good. ﴿Indeed, He is Aware of what you do.﴾ The people of Kufa recited "taf'aluna" with the ta', and others with the ya'. Abu 'Ubayda chose the ya' with the statement "atawhu," since it is a report about them.

﴿Whoever comes with good﴾ — meaning whoever arrives before God with faith. Abu Ma'shar said: Ibrahim used to swear without any exception that the good deed is: "There is no god but God." Qatada said: with sincerity.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Shanbah told us, saying: 'Ubayd [in the second copy: 'Abd] Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Mansur told us, saying: Sahl ibn Bishr told us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Sulayman told us, saying: Sa'd ibn Sa'id told us, saying: I heard 'Ali ibn al-Husayn say: A man went out to fight in the way of God, and whenever he was alone in a place he would say: "There is no god but God, alone, without partner." Then one day, while he was in the land of the Romans, in a place of reeds and dry grass, he raised his voice saying: "There is no god but God, alone, without partner." A man came out to him on a horse, wearing white garments, and said: "O servant of God, what is this you have said?" He said: "I said what you heard. By Him in whose hand my soul is, it is the word of which God, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Whoever comes with good﴾."

﴿Then he will have better than it, and they will be secure from the terror of that Day.﴾

Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-'Abbasi informed me, saying: al-Qadi Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn 'Uthman [al-Nasibi in Baghdad] informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Subay'i told us in Aleppo, saying: al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim al-Jassas told me, saying: al-Husayn ibn al-Hakam informed us, saying: Isma'il ibn Aban told us, from [Fudayl] ibn al-Zubayr, from Abu Dawud al-Subay'i, from Abu 'Abd Allah al-Hudhali, who said: I entered upon 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and he said: "O servant of God, shall I tell you of the good deed, whoever comes with which God will admit into Paradise, and of the evil deed, whoever comes with which God will hurl him into the Fire, and no deed will be accepted with it?"

I said: Yes. He said: "The good deed is our love, and the evil deed is our hatred."

﴿Then he will have better than it﴾ — that is, from this good deed he will have better on the Day of Resurrection, which is the reward and security from punishment.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿Then he will have better than it﴾ means that from it good reaches him. Al-Hasan said: its meaning is that he has good from it. 'Ikrima and Ibn Jurayj said: As for whether he has better than faith, no. There is nothing better than "There is no god but God," but he has good from it. Ibn 'Abbas also said: ﴿Then he will have better than it﴾ means the reward, because obedience is the servant's action and the reward is God's action, glory be to Him.

It has been said: God, Mighty and Majestic, accepts his faith and his good deeds, and God's acceptance is better than the servant's deed. It has also been said: ﴿Then he will have better than it﴾ means the good pleasure of God, glory be to Him. God, may He be exalted, says: ﴿And the good pleasure of God is greater.﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 72.]

Muhammad ibn Ka'b and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: ﴿Then he will have better than it﴾ means the multiplication. God gives the good deed as ten times over, and so this is better than it. Ibn Ka'b and Ibn Zayd were right in their interpretations, because multiplication has distinctive features: the servant is questioned about his deed but is not questioned about the multiplication; Satan has a path to his deed but has no path to the multiplication; the adversaries have no hope in the multiplication; the abode of the good deed is this world, and the abode of multiplication is Paradise; and Paradise is by the servant's merit, while multiplication is as befits the generosity of the Lord.

﴿And they will be secure from the terror of that Day.﴾ The people of Kufa recited "fazi'in" with tanwin and "yawma'idhin" with a fatha on the mim, which is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud. The rest of the reciters read it with the genitive construction. Abu 'Ubayd chose it, saying: because it is the more general of the two interpretations, that security is from all the terror of that Day. But if one says "min fazi'a yawma'idhin," it becomes as though it were a terror of a particular kind. Al-Farra' also chose this, saying: because it is a known terror. Do you not see that He said: ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾? So He made it definite. If you give it the genitive construction, it becomes definite, and this is more pleasing to me.

﴿And whoever comes with evil﴾ — meaning association with partners.

Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, saying: Makki ibn 'Abdan informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Hashim told us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman told us, from Sufyan, from Abu al-Mahjal, from Abu Ma'shar, from Ibrahim, concerning ﴿whoever comes with good﴾, he said: "There is no god but God." And ﴿whoever comes with evil﴾, he said: "Association with partners."

'Abd ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb al-Bayhaqi informed us, saying: Bishr ibn Musa told us, saying: Rawh told us, from Habib ibn al-Shahid, from al-Hasan, who said: The price of Paradise is "There is no god but God."

﴿So their faces will be thrown into the Fire.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: they will be cast down. Al-Dahhak said: they will be flung. Abu al-'Aliya said: they will be overturned. It has been said that they will be told: ﴿Are you recompensed except for what you used to do?﴾

God, glory be to Him, says to His Prophet, Muhammad (peace be upon him): Say: ﴿I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city, which He has made sacred,﴾ meaning Makkah, which He made a sanctuary and a place of safety. Shedding blood unlawfully is not permitted in it, no one is wronged in it, it is not to be hunted, its game is not to be hunted, and its plants are not to be cut. Ibn 'Abbas recited "allati harramaha" (which He has made sacred), referring to the city.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 27, verse 83–93 (part 2 of 2):

﴿And His is every thing, by creation and by ownership.﴾ ﴿I have been commanded to be among the Muslims, and to recite the Qur'an. So whoever is guided, he is only guided for his own soul; and whoever goes astray, say: I am only one of the warners.﴾ ﴿And upon us is only the conveyance (of the message).﴾ [[Surat Ya-Sin: 17.]] It was abrogated by the verse of fighting (naskh, abrogation: the replacement of a earlier ruling by a later one).

﴿And say: Praise belongs to Allah﴾ for His blessings. ﴿He will show you His signs﴾, meaning on the Day of Badr. Its parallel is in Surat al-Anbiya': ﴿I will show you My signs, so do not seek to hasten them.﴾

Mujahid said: ﴿He will show you His signs﴾ within yourselves, in the heavens and the earth, and in provision. His proof is His saying: ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves﴾ [[Surat Fussilat: 53.]] and His saying: ﴿And on the earth are signs for those who are certain, and within yourselves﴾ [[Surat adh-Dhariyat: 20–21.]] ﴿So you will recognize them.﴾ ﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what you do.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 27, verses 83–93 (part 1 of 2):

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And on the Day when We shall gather from every nation a troop of those who denied Our signs, and they will be driven in ranks.﴾ A group of those who deny. Their first is held back until their last, so that they gather together, and then they are driven to the Fire. Ibn 'Abbas said: "yuza'un" means they are pushed. ﴿Until, when they have come, He will say: "Did you deny My signs without comprehending them in knowledge, or what was it that you were doing?"﴾ God, glory be to Him, says to them: Did you deny My signs without having encompassed them in knowledge, and without having known their true knowing? "Or what was it that you were doing" regarding them, by denial or by affirmation? It has also been said that this is a rebuke: what were you doing when you did not search into them and did not reflect upon them? ﴿And the word will fall upon them because of their wrongdoing,﴾ meaning the punishment becomes due because they associated partners, ﴿so they will not speak.﴾ Because their mouths will be sealed. Most of the exegetes said: "so they will not speak" with a proof or an excuse. Its parallel is the saying of God, glory be to Him: ﴿This is a day on which they will not speak, nor will they be permitted to make excuses.﴾ [Surah al-Mursalat: 35–36.] ﴿Have they not seen that We made the night for them to rest therein, and the day giving sight? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ Those who affirm and so take heed. The words of the Exalted: ﴿And on the Day when the Trumpet is blown﴾ — this is the first blast.

Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Yazid al-Sayrafi informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn Harb told us, saying: Asbat told us, saying: Salman al-Tamimi [in the second copy: al-Taymi] told us, from Aslam al-'Ijli, from Bishr ibn Shaghaf, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: A Bedouin came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and asked him about the Sur, and he said: "A horn into which it is blown." [Musnad Ahmad: 2/162.] [121].

Mujahid said: the Sur is like the shape of a trumpet. It has also been said that it is in the language of the people of Yemen, and most of the exegetes hold this view. What supports it is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "How can I be at ease, when the holder of the horn has put the horn to his mouth and bowed his forehead, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow?" [Kanz al-'Ummal: 14/625, no. 39743.] [122].

Qatada and Abu 'Ubaida said: it is the plural of "surah" (form), one says "surah" and "sur," and "sur" is like the "sur" of a building or a mosque, and its plural is "sur" and "su'ur." Abu 'Ubaida recited:
"I travelled towards her on the high parts of the walls."
So the meaning of the verse is: and the forms of creation are blown.

A comprehensive and sound report has come concerning the manner of the blowing of the Sur, which is what:

Imam Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Mihrajani informed us by reading to him, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim al-Shafi'i in Baghdad, saying: Abu Qilaba al-Raqqashi informed me, saying: Abu 'Asim al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad informed me, from Isma'il ibn Rafi', from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from a man of the Ansar, from Abu Hurayra, who said:

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When God, Mighty and Majestic, finished creating the heavens and the earth, He created the Sur and gave it to Israfil, who placed it at his mouth, his gaze fixed on the Plain, waiting for when he will be told."

I said: O Messenger of God, what is the Sur? He said: "The horn." I said: What is it like? He said: "Great. By Him who sent me with the truth, its width is like the breadth of the heavens and the earth. It is blown with three blasts: the first is the blast of terror, the second is the blast of swooning, and the third is the blast of rising for the Lord of the worlds. God, Mighty and Majestic, commands Israfil (peace be upon him) concerning the first blast, and he says: 'Blow the blast of terror,' and so those in the heavens and the earth are terrified, except whom God wills. He commands him, and he prolongs it and extends it. This is what God, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿They await only one shout, with no pause.﴾ God sets the mountains in motion, so they pass like clouds and become a mirage. The earth is shaken with its inhabitants with a violent shaking, so it is like a ship moored in the sea, struck by the waves and tossed by the winds, or like a lamp hanging from the Throne, swayed by the winds. This is what God, Mighty and Majestic, refers to in His words: ﴿On the Day when the Quaker quakes, followed by the Follower; hearts on that day will be trembling.﴾ Then the earth stretches out with the people upon its back. Nursing women forget their infants, pregnant women give birth, children turn grey, and the devils flee in terror until they reach the horizons, where the angels meet them and strike their faces. They turn back, and the people flee in retreat, calling out to one another. This is what God, Mighty and Majestic, refers to in His words: ﴿The Day of Calling out, the Day when you turn your backs and flee; you will have no protector from God.﴾"

"While they are in this state, the earth splits open from one side to another, or they see a great matter the like of which they have never seen, and the anguish and terror that God alone knows seize them. Then they look at the sky, and it is like molten brass. Then it is split open, its stars scattered and its sun and moon eclipsed."

He (ﷺ) said: "Those are the martyrs. Terror reaches only the living, and they are alive with their Lord, being provided for. God protected them from the terror of that Day and made them secure. It is a punishment God sends upon the worst of His creation. This is what God refers to when He says: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord; indeed, the quaking of the Hour is a tremendous thing,﴾ up to His words: ﴿But the punishment of God is severe.﴾"

He says: "You remain, the Living who does not die, and the bearers of Your Throne remain, and I remain." He says: "Let the bearers of My Throne die," and they die. Then God commands the Throne, and it takes the Sur from Israfil, and he dies.

Then the Angel of Death comes and says: "O Lord, the bearers of Your Throne have died." He says, and He knows best who remains: "Who remains?" He says: "You remain, the Living who does not die, and I remain." He says: "You are a creature among My creatures, whom I created for a purpose. Die," and he dies. When no one remains but God, the One, the Unique, the Eternal Refuge, ﴿who begets not, nor is He begotten, and none is comparable to Him﴾, and He was the last as He was the first, He folds up the heavens ﴿like the folding of a scroll for writings.﴾

"Ṣun'a Allah" (the work of God) is in the accusative as a verbal noun. It has also been said that it is in the accusative as an incitement, meaning: know and see ﴿the work of God, who perfected everything.﴾ That is, He made everything firm. Qatada said: He made everything good. ﴿Indeed, He is Aware of what you do.﴾ The people of Kufa recited "taf'aluna" with the ta', and others with the ya'. Abu 'Ubayda chose the ya' with the statement "atawhu," since it is a report about them.

﴿Whoever comes with good﴾ — meaning whoever arrives before God with faith. Abu Ma'shar said: Ibrahim used to swear without any exception that the good deed is: "There is no god but God." Qatada said: with sincerity.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Shanbah told us, saying: 'Ubayd [in the second copy: 'Abd] Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Mansur told us, saying: Sahl ibn Bishr told us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Sulayman told us, saying: Sa'd ibn Sa'id told us, saying: I heard 'Ali ibn al-Husayn say: A man went out to fight in the way of God, and whenever he was alone in a place he would say: "There is no god but God, alone, without partner." Then one day, while he was in the land of the Romans, in a place of reeds and dry grass, he raised his voice saying: "There is no god but God, alone, without partner." A man came out to him on a horse, wearing white garments, and said: "O servant of God, what is this you have said?" He said: "I said what you heard. By Him in whose hand my soul is, it is the word of which God, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Whoever comes with good﴾."

﴿Then he will have better than it, and they will be secure from the terror of that Day.﴾

Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-'Abbasi informed me, saying: al-Qadi Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn 'Uthman [al-Nasibi in Baghdad] informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Subay'i told us in Aleppo, saying: al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim al-Jassas told me, saying: al-Husayn ibn al-Hakam informed us, saying: Isma'il ibn Aban told us, from [Fudayl] ibn al-Zubayr, from Abu Dawud al-Subay'i, from Abu 'Abd Allah al-Hudhali, who said: I entered upon 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and he said: "O servant of God, shall I tell you of the good deed, whoever comes with which God will admit into Paradise, and of the evil deed, whoever comes with which God will hurl him into the Fire, and no deed will be accepted with it?"

I said: Yes. He said: "The good deed is our love, and the evil deed is our hatred."

﴿Then he will have better than it﴾ — that is, from this good deed he will have better on the Day of Resurrection, which is the reward and security from punishment.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿Then he will have better than it﴾ means that from it good reaches him. Al-Hasan said: its meaning is that he has good from it. 'Ikrima and Ibn Jurayj said: As for whether he has better than faith, no. There is nothing better than "There is no god but God," but he has good from it. Ibn 'Abbas also said: ﴿Then he will have better than it﴾ means the reward, because obedience is the servant's action and the reward is God's action, glory be to Him.

It has been said: God, Mighty and Majestic, accepts his faith and his good deeds, and God's acceptance is better than the servant's deed. It has also been said: ﴿Then he will have better than it﴾ means the good pleasure of God, glory be to Him. God, may He be exalted, says: ﴿And the good pleasure of God is greater.﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 72.]

Muhammad ibn Ka'b and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: ﴿Then he will have better than it﴾ means the multiplication. God gives the good deed as ten times over, and so this is better than it. Ibn Ka'b and Ibn Zayd were right in their interpretations, because multiplication has distinctive features: the servant is questioned about his deed but is not questioned about the multiplication; Satan has a path to his deed but has no path to the multiplication; the adversaries have no hope in the multiplication; the abode of the good deed is this world, and the abode of multiplication is Paradise; and Paradise is by the servant's merit, while multiplication is as befits the generosity of the Lord.

﴿And they will be secure from the terror of that Day.﴾ The people of Kufa recited "fazi'in" with tanwin and "yawma'idhin" with a fatha on the mim, which is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud. The rest of the reciters read it with the genitive construction. Abu 'Ubayd chose it, saying: because it is the more general of the two interpretations, that security is from all the terror of that Day. But if one says "min fazi'a yawma'idhin," it becomes as though it were a terror of a particular kind. Al-Farra' also chose this, saying: because it is a known terror. Do you not see that He said: ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾? So He made it definite. If you give it the genitive construction, it becomes definite, and this is more pleasing to me.

﴿And whoever comes with evil﴾ — meaning association with partners.

Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, saying: Makki ibn 'Abdan informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Hashim told us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman told us, from Sufyan, from Abu al-Mahjal, from Abu Ma'shar, from Ibrahim, concerning ﴿whoever comes with good﴾, he said: "There is no god but God." And ﴿whoever comes with evil﴾, he said: "Association with partners."

'Abd ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb al-Bayhaqi informed us, saying: Bishr ibn Musa told us, saying: Rawh told us, from Habib ibn al-Shahid, from al-Hasan, who said: The price of Paradise is "There is no god but God."

﴿So their faces will be thrown into the Fire.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: they will be cast down. Al-Dahhak said: they will be flung. Abu al-'Aliya said: they will be overturned. It has been said that they will be told: ﴿Are you recompensed except for what you used to do?﴾

God, glory be to Him, says to His Prophet, Muhammad (peace be upon him): Say: ﴿I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city, which He has made sacred,﴾ meaning Makkah, which He made a sanctuary and a place of safety. Shedding blood unlawfully is not permitted in it, no one is wronged in it, it is not to be hunted, its game is not to be hunted, and its plants are not to be cut. Ibn 'Abbas recited "allati harramaha" (which He has made sacred), referring to the city.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 27, verse 83–93 (part 2 of 2):

﴿And His is every thing, by creation and by ownership.﴾ ﴿I have been commanded to be among the Muslims, and to recite the Qur'an. So whoever is guided, he is only guided for his own soul; and whoever goes astray, say: I am only one of the warners.﴾ ﴿And upon us is only the conveyance (of the message).﴾ [[Surat Ya-Sin: 17.]] It was abrogated by the verse of fighting (naskh, abrogation: the replacement of a earlier ruling by a later one).

﴿And say: Praise belongs to Allah﴾ for His blessings. ﴿He will show you His signs﴾, meaning on the Day of Badr. Its parallel is in Surat al-Anbiya': ﴿I will show you My signs, so do not seek to hasten them.﴾

Mujahid said: ﴿He will show you His signs﴾ within yourselves, in the heavens and the earth, and in provision. His proof is His saying: ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves﴾ [[Surat Fussilat: 53.]] and His saying: ﴿And on the earth are signs for those who are certain, and within yourselves﴾ [[Surat adh-Dhariyat: 20–21.]] ﴿So you will recognize them.﴾ ﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what you do.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 27, verses 83–93 (part 1 of 2):

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And on the Day when We shall gather from every nation a troop of those who denied Our signs, and they will be driven in ranks.﴾ A group of those who deny. Their first is held back until their last, so that they gather together, and then they are driven to the Fire. Ibn 'Abbas said: "yuza'un" means they are pushed. ﴿Until, when they have come, He will say: "Did you deny My signs without comprehending them in knowledge, or what was it that you were doing?"﴾ God, glory be to Him, says to them: Did you deny My signs without having encompassed them in knowledge, and without having known their true knowing? "Or what was it that you were doing" regarding them, by denial or by affirmation? It has also been said that this is a rebuke: what were you doing when you did not search into them and did not reflect upon them? ﴿And the word will fall upon them because of their wrongdoing,﴾ meaning the punishment becomes due because they associated partners, ﴿so they will not speak.﴾ Because their mouths will be sealed. Most of the exegetes said: "so they will not speak" with a proof or an excuse. Its parallel is the saying of God, glory be to Him: ﴿This is a day on which they will not speak, nor will they be permitted to make excuses.﴾ [Surah al-Mursalat: 35–36.] ﴿Have they not seen that We made the night for them to rest therein, and the day giving sight? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ Those who affirm and so take heed. The words of the Exalted: ﴿And on the Day when the Trumpet is blown﴾ — this is the first blast.

Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Yazid al-Sayrafi informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn Harb told us, saying: Asbat told us, saying: Salman al-Tamimi [in the second copy: al-Taymi] told us, from Aslam al-'Ijli, from Bishr ibn Shaghaf, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: A Bedouin came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and asked him about the Sur, and he said: "A horn into which it is blown." [Musnad Ahmad: 2/162.] [121].

Mujahid said: the Sur is like the shape of a trumpet. It has also been said that it is in the language of the people of Yemen, and most of the exegetes hold this view. What supports it is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "How can I be at ease, when the holder of the horn has put the horn to his mouth and bowed his forehead, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow?" [Kanz al-'Ummal: 14/625, no. 39743.] [122].

Qatada and Abu 'Ubaida said: it is the plural of "surah" (form), one says "surah" and "sur," and "sur" is like the "sur" of a building or a mosque, and its plural is "sur" and "su'ur." Abu 'Ubaida recited:
"I travelled towards her on the high parts of the walls."
So the meaning of the verse is: and the forms of creation are blown.

A comprehensive and sound report has come concerning the manner of the blowing of the Sur, which is what:

Imam Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Mihrajani informed us by reading to him, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim al-Shafi'i in Baghdad, saying: Abu Qilaba al-Raqqashi informed me, saying: Abu 'Asim al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad informed me, from Isma'il ibn Rafi', from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from a man of the Ansar, from Abu Hurayra, who said:

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When God, Mighty and Majestic, finished creating the heavens and the earth, He created the Sur and gave it to Israfil, who placed it at his mouth, his gaze fixed on the Plain, waiting for when he will be told."

I said: O Messenger of God, what is the Sur? He said: "The horn." I said: What is it like? He said: "Great. By Him who sent me with the truth, its width is like the breadth of the heavens and the earth. It is blown with three blasts: the first is the blast of terror, the second is the blast of swooning, and the third is the blast of rising for the Lord of the worlds. God, Mighty and Majestic, commands Israfil (peace be upon him) concerning the first blast, and he says: 'Blow the blast of terror,' and so those in the heavens and the earth are terrified, except whom God wills. He commands him, and he prolongs it and extends it. This is what God, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿They await only one shout, with no pause.﴾ God sets the mountains in motion, so they pass like clouds and become a mirage. The earth is shaken with its inhabitants with a violent shaking, so it is like a ship moored in the sea, struck by the waves and tossed by the winds, or like a lamp hanging from the Throne, swayed by the winds. This is what God, Mighty and Majestic, refers to in His words: ﴿On the Day when the Quaker quakes, followed by the Follower; hearts on that day will be trembling.﴾ Then the earth stretches out with the people upon its back. Nursing women forget their infants, pregnant women give birth, children turn grey, and the devils flee in terror until they reach the horizons, where the angels meet them and strike their faces. They turn back, and the people flee in retreat, calling out to one another. This is what God, Mighty and Majestic, refers to in His words: ﴿The Day of Calling out, the Day when you turn your backs and flee; you will have no protector from God.﴾"

"While they are in this state, the earth splits open from one side to another, or they see a great matter the like of which they have never seen, and the anguish and terror that God alone knows seize them. Then they look at the sky, and it is like molten brass. Then it is split open, its stars scattered and its sun and moon eclipsed."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The dead on that day will know something of that." [123].

Abu Hurayra said: O Messenger of God, who is it that God excepted when He said: ﴿And whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified, except whom God wills﴾?

He (ﷺ) said: "Those are the martyrs. Terror reaches only the living, and they are alive with their Lord, being provided for. God protected them from the terror of that Day and made them secure. It is a punishment God sends upon the worst of His creation. This is what God refers to when He says: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord; indeed, the quaking of the Hour is a tremendous thing,﴾ up to His words: ﴿But the punishment of God is severe.﴾"

They remain in that affliction as long as God wills, except that it lasts long for them. Then God commands Israfil, and he blows the blast of swooning, and ﴿whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth swoons, except whom God wills.﴾ When they are gathered, the Angel of Death comes to the Almighty and says: "The people of the heavens and the earth have died, except whom You will." God, glory be to Him, who knows best, says: "Who remains?" He says: "O Lord, You remain, the Living who does not die. The bearers of the Throne remain, Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil remain, and I remain." God says: "Jibril and Mika'il will die." So they die. Then the Throne speaks and says: "O Lord, will Jibril and Mika'il die?" He says: "Be silent. I have decreed death upon everyone beneath My Throne, and so they will die."

Then the Angel of Death comes and says: "O Lord, Jibril and Mika'il have died." He says, and He knows best who remains: "Who remains?" He says: "You remain, the Living who does not die, and the bearers of Your Throne remain, and I remain." He says: "Let the bearers of My Throne die," and they die. Then God commands the Throne, and it takes the Sur from Israfil, and he dies.

Then the Angel of Death comes and says: "O Lord, the bearers of Your Throne have died." He says, and He knows best who remains: "Who remains?" He says: "You remain, the Living who does not die, and I remain." He says: "You are a creature among My creatures, whom I created for a purpose. Die," and he dies. When no one remains but God, the One, the Unique, the Eternal Refuge, ﴿who begets not, nor is He begotten, and none is comparable to Him﴾, and He was the last as He was the first, He folds up the heavens ﴿like the folding of a scroll for writings.﴾

Then He says: "I am the Almighty. ﴿To whom belongs the dominion this Day?﴾" and no one answers Him. Then He, blessed and exalted, glorified in His names, says: ﴿To God, the One, the Subduer.﴾ ﴿The Day the earth will be changed into another earth﴾ ﴿and the heavens folded up.﴾ He spreads them out in a spreading, then stretches them like a tanned hide, ﴿in which you will see no crookedness or unevenness.﴾

Then God drives the creatures with one driving, and they are in this changed earth in the same state they were in at first: whoever was in its belly is in its belly, and whoever was on its back is on its back. Then God sends down upon them water from beneath the Throne like the semen of men, and then He commands the clouds to send down rain for forty days, until it reaches twelve cubits above them. God, glory be to Him, commands the bodies to grow like the growth of the truffles and the growth of herbs, until their bodies are complete as they were. God, glory be to Him, says: "Let the bearers of the Throne live," and they live. Then God, may He be exalted, says: "Let Jibril and Mika'il live," and they live. Then God commands Israfil, and he takes the Sur and places it at his mouth. Then God calls the souls and they are brought; the souls of the believers shine with light, and the others are dark. He seizes them all and then casts them into the Sur. Then God, glory be to Him, commands Israfil to blow a blast for the Resurrection, and the souls come out like bees that have filled what is in the heavens and the earth. God, glory be to Him, says: "Every soul shall return to its body," and the souls enter the nostrils, and then they move through the bodies as poison moves through one who has been stung.

Then the earth splits open over them swiftly. I am the first whom the earth splits open for. You will come out of it to your Lord, hastening, naked, barefoot, uncircumcised, ﴿hurrying toward the summoner.﴾ The disbelievers will say: "This is a difficult day." [124].

The words of the Exalted: ﴿So they are terrified﴾ — meaning "so they will be terrified." The Arabs do this in places where "idha" (when) fits, because "idha" is followed by a verb in the past or the present, as in your saying: "I will visit you when you visit me" and "I will visit you when you are visiting me." ﴿Whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, except whom God wills﴾ — that they not be terrified. We have already mentioned in the preceding report that they are the martyrs. ﴿And all come to Him, humbled.﴾ Al-A'mash, Hamza, Khalaf and Hafs recited "atawhu" with a short vowel, as a finite verb meaning "they came to Him," coordinated with His words "fa-fazi'a" (so they were terrified), and "atawhu" following the reading of Ibn Mas'ud.

Muhammad ibn Nu'aym informed us, saying: al-Husayn [in the second copy: al-Hasan] ibn Ayyub told us, saying: 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz told us, saying: Abu 'Ubayd told us, saying: Hisham told us, from Mughira, from Ibrahim. And Muhammad ibn 'Abdus informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Jahm told us, saying: al-Farra' told us, saying: 'Iddah (a number of people) told me, among them al-Mufaddal al-Dabbi, Qays and Abu Bakr, all from Jahsh ibn Ziyad al-Dabbi, both from Tamim ibn Hudhlam, who said: I recited to 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud "wa-kullun atawhu dakhirin" with a lengthened alif, and he said: "wa-kullun atawhu" with a short vowel.

The rest of the reciters recited with the lengthening of the alif and a damma on the ta', in the pattern of "fa'iluhu," as in His words: ﴿And every one of them will come to Him alone on the Day of Resurrection.﴾ [Surah Maryam: 95.] This is the reading of 'Ali, may God be pleased with him.

"Dakhirin" means humbled.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And you will see the mountains﴾ — O Muhammad — ﴿you think them fixed,﴾ standing, stationary, settled in their place. ﴿Yet they pass by as the clouds pass.﴾ When they strike the earth, they level it with them.

Al-Qutaybi said: That is because the mountains are gathered and move, and in the sight of the eye they appear to be standing while they are moving. Likewise, everything great and every large gathering that the eye cannot take in, because of its multitude and immensity, and whose extremities are counted, appears to the observer to be standing still while it is moving. The poet referred to this in describing an army:
"O troop, like a mountain you think them standing still for a halt, while the riding camels pace."

﴿And say: Praise belongs to Allah﴾ for His blessings. ﴿He will show you His signs﴾, meaning on the Day of Badr. Its parallel is in Surat al-Anbiya': ﴿I will show you My signs, so do not seek to hasten them.﴾

Mujahid said: ﴿He will show you His signs﴾ within yourselves, in the heavens and the earth, and in provision. His proof is His saying: ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves﴾ [[Surat Fussilat: 53.]] and His saying: ﴿And on the earth are signs for those who are certain, and within yourselves﴾ [[Surat adh-Dhariyat: 20–21.]] ﴿So you will recognize them.﴾ ﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what you do.﴾
